title: حِكَايَةُ نُورِ الدِّينِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْفَضْلِ وَأَنِيسِ الْجَلِيسِ
titleEn: The Tale of the Two Viziers and Anīs al-Jalīs, continued
part: Night 37 · The Two Viziers and Anīs al-Jalīs, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 301–312 (Night 37, continuing directly from nights-36), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 37 continues the tale of Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī and Anīs al-Jalīs. The candles and lamps of the garden pavilion catch the eye of the caliph Hārūn al-Rashīd, who storms at his vizier Jaʿfar, goes with him in disguise to the garden, and watches the revellers from a walnut tree; he then takes the clothes of a fisherman, Karīm, fries fish for the company, and hears the slave-girl's songs and Nūr al-Dīn's verses, as the night breaks off with the caliph promising Nūr al-Dīn a letter of recommendation to the sultan Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Zaynī. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّابِعَةُ وَالثَّلَٰثُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-sābiʿatu wa-al-thalāthūna
sentences.l: And when the night came to be, the night, the seventh and the thirty,
sentences.i: When the thirty-seventh night came,
sentences.n: As on the previous nights, the print has الثلثون without the alif of ثلاثون; it is kept as printed, with the dagger alif marking the missing long ā. Here فلما and كانت are printed as two words.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ نُورَالدِّينِ عَلِيَّ قَامَ وَقَعَدَ عَلَى حَيْلِهِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna Nūra al-Dīni ʿAliyya qāma wa-qaʿada ʿalā ḥaylihi
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king, the happy one, that Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī stood and sat upon his strength.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī rose and sat down again, pulling himself together.
sentences.n: The speaker is Shahrazād, resuming the tale where the last night broke off: the party is in Shaykh Ibrāhīm's garden pavilion, and Nūr al-Dīn has just been trying to make the old man drink. The print has علي with no alif, so I vocalise the accusative as ʿAliyya (fatḥa on the shadda) rather than ʿAliyyan. على حيله is idiomatic and I am not sure of it: I read حَيْل, “strength, vigour”, so “he stood and sat on his own strength”, that is, he roused himself; حِيلَة, “stratagem”, is the other possibility.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا شَيْخَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ أَيْشْ هَذَا أَنَا مَا حَلَفْتُ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ سَاعَةٍ فَأَبَيْتَ وَقُلْتَ أَنَا لِي ثَلَٰثَةَ عَشَرَ سَنَةً مَا فَعَلْتُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā shaykha Ibrāhīma aysh hādhā anā mā ḥalaftu ʿalayka min sāʿatin fa-abayta wa-qulta anā lī thalāthata ʿashara sanatan mā faʿaltuhu
sentences.l: And he said to him: O shaykh Ibrāhīm, what (is) this? I — did I not swear upon you since an hour, and you refused, and you said: I, to-me (are) thirteen years, I have-not done-it?
sentences.i: He said to him, “Shaykh Ibrāhīm, what is this? Did I not swear an oath upon you an hour ago, and you refused, and said, ‘It is thirteen years since I did that’?”
sentences.n: أيش (“what?”) is the colloquial form of أيّ شيء and recurs throughout; I write it with a final sukun. ما حلفت … من ساعة is a colloquial question without a question particle: “Did I not swear … an hour ago?”, the oath being the one by which Nūr al-Dīn tried to make the shaykh drink. The shaykh's reported words, أنا لي ثلثة عشر سنة ما فعلته, are “I, I have (had) thirteen years (that) I have not done it”; the print has no alif on سنة, and I give the Classical accusative singular after the number.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ وَقَدِ اسْتَحْيَى وَاللَّهِ مَالِي ذَنْبٌ إِلَّا هِيَ قَالَتْ لِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu wa-qadi istaḥyā wa-Allāhi mā-lī dhanbun illā hiya qālat lī
sentences.l: And said the shaykh Ibrāhīm — and he had been-ashamed —: By God, no-fault-to-me except she: she said to me.
sentences.i: Shaykh Ibrāhīm, who had grown ashamed, said, “By God, the fault is none of mine but hers: it was she who spoke to me.”
sentences.n: The sentence breaks off where the print leaves it: “she said to me …” — what she said is not given, and the next sentence moves on to Nūr al-Dīn laughing. The shaykh is shifting the blame onto the girl, who had evidently urged him to drink; I do not supply the missing words. مالي is printed as one word, mā-lī, “I have no”. استحيى is the print's spelling, with final ى, of استحيا.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ نُورُالدِّينِ وَقَعَدُوا لِلْمُنَادَمَهْ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika Nūru al-Dīni wa-qaʿadū li-al-munādamah
sentences.l: And laughed Nūr al-Dīn, and they sat for-the-carousing.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn laughed, and they settled down to their carousing.
sentences.n: The print spells المنادمة with a final ه, as a tāʾ marbūṭa is often written in Middle Arabic; I vocalise it as ‑ah with a sukun, which is how it was spoken. The same word appears again below with the ة.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ وَقَالَتْ لِسَيِّدِهَا سِرًّا فِيمَا بَيْنَهُمَا يَا سَيِّدِي اشْرَبْ وَلَا تَحْلِفْ عَلَى الشَّيْخِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَتَّى أُفَرِّجَكَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-iltafatati al-jāriyatu wa-qālat li-sayyidihā sirran fīmā baynahumā yā sayyidī ishrab wa-lā taḥlif ʿalā al-shaykhi Ibrāhīma ḥattā ufarrijaka ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And turned the slave-girl and said to her master, secretly, in-what (was) between the-two-of-them: O my master, drink, and do not swear upon the shaykh Ibrāhīm, until I make-you-see (a show) upon him.
sentences.i: The girl turned and said to her master, in secret, between the two of them, “My lord, drink, and do not press the shaykh with oaths, until I give you a good show at his expense.”
sentences.n: The print has a full stop after عليه; the sentence is one and the stop is not reproduced. حلف على فلان is “to swear upon someone”, that is, to bind him by an oath to do something. أفرّجك عليه is colloquial “I will let you watch (a spectacle) at his expense”: the girl has a plan for amusing Nūr al-Dīn with the old man. Note the subjunctive after حتى, which the text keeps.

sentences.t: فَجَعَلَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ تَمْلَأُ وَتَسْقِي سَيِّدَهَا وَسَيِّدُهَا يَمْلَأُ وَيَسْقِيهَا وَلَمْ يَزَالَا كَذَلِكَ مَرَّةً بَعْدَ مَرَّةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-jaʿalati al-jāriyatu tamlaʾu wa-tasqī sayyidahā wa-sayyiduhā yamlaʾu wa-yasqīhā wa-lam yazālā ka-dhālika marratan baʿda marratin
sentences.l: And began the slave-girl (to) fill and give-to-drink her master, and her master fills and gives-her-to-drink, and the-two-of-them did not cease thus, time after time.
sentences.i: The girl began to fill the cup and give her master to drink, and her master filled it and gave her to drink, and so they went on, round after round.
sentences.n: جعل + present verb is “began to …”. The print gives تملأ and يملأ with the hamza already written on the alif, so those two are kept precomposed. The phrase ولم يزالا كذلك has the Classical dual jussive, agreeing with the pair.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ لَهُمَا الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ وَقَالَ لَهُمَا أَيْشْ هَذِهِ الْمُعَاشَرَةُ لَعَنَ اللَّهُ مَنْ فِيهَا بَطْنًا فِي دُورِنَا مَا تَسْقِينِي يَا أَخِي أَيْشْ هَذَا الْحَالُ يَا مُبَارَكُ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara lahumā al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu wa-qāla lahumā aysh hādhihi al-muʿāsharatu laʿana Allāhu man fīhā baṭnan fī dūrinā mā tasqīnī yā akhī aysh hādhā al-ḥālu yā mubārak
sentences.l: And looked at-the-two-of-them the shaykh Ibrāhīm and said to-them: What (is) this companionship? May God curse whoever (is) in it, (as to) belly, in our houses. Do you not give-me-to-drink, O my brother? What (is) this state of-things, O blessed one?
sentences.i: Shaykh Ibrāhīm looked at them and said, “What sort of company is this? God curse everyone in it, bellies and all, in our own houses! Will you not give me something to drink, my brother? What a way to go on, my good fellow!”
sentences.n: This outburst is obscure in places. لعن الله من فيها بطنا في دورنا is, word for word, “God curse whoever is in it — belly — in our houses”; بطنا may be an accusative of respect (“as to the belly”) or a stock expression for “one and all”, and I give both in the idiomatic layer without being sure of either. ما تسقيني is a reproachful question, “aren't you going to give me a drink?”. يا مبارك is a friendly, half-teasing address, “my good man”.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَا مِنْ كَلَامِهِ حَتَّى اسْتَلْقَيَا عَلَى ظُهُورِهِمَا ثُمَّ شَرِبَا وَسَقَيَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥikā min kalāmihi ḥattā istalqayā ʿalā ẓuhūrihimā thumma sharibā wa-saqayāhu
sentences.l: And the-two-of-them laughed at his speech until they lay-back upon their backs; then they-two drank, and gave-him-to-drink.
sentences.i: They laughed at his words until they fell on their backs, and then they drank and gave him to drink also.

sentences.t: وَلَا زَالُوا فِى الْمُنَادَمَةِ إِلَى ثُلُثِ اللَّيْلِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā zālū fī al-munādamati ilā thuluthi al-layli
sentences.l: And they did not cease in the carousing until a-third of-the-night.
sentences.i: And they went on with their carousing until a third of the night had passed.
sentences.n: The print has the dotless spelling فى for في, which is kept. ولا زالوا, with the plural, now takes in all three; the earlier dual was for the pair alone.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ قَالَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ يَا شَيْخَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ إِذْنِكَ هَلْ أَقُومُ وَأُوقِدُ شَمْعَةً مِنْ هَذَا الشَّمْعِ الْمَصْفُوفِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika qālati al-jāriyatu yā shaykha Ibrāhīma ʿan idhnika hal aqūmu wa-ūqidu shamʿatan min hādhā al-shamʿi al-maṣfūfi
sentences.l: And at that, said the slave-girl: O shaykh Ibrāhīm, with your leave, shall I rise and light a candle from this candle-stuff, the ranged?
sentences.i: At that the girl said, “Shaykh Ibrāhīm, with your leave, may I get up and light one of these candles, set out in their rows?”
sentences.n: عن إذنك is the polite “with your permission”. أقوم وأوقد are indicative, as in colloquial speech, where Classical would have the subjunctive after هل.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَهَا قُومِي وَلَا تُوقِدِي إِلَّا شَمْعَةً وَاحِدَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ahā qūmī wa-lā tūqidī illā shamʿatan wāḥidatan
sentences.l: And he said: Aha! Rise, and do not light except one candle.
sentences.i: He said, “Aha! Up with you, but light only a single candle.”
sentences.n: أها is an interjection of assent or mock-grudging consent; there is no exact Classical equivalent.

sentences.t: فَنَهَضَتْ عَلَى قَدَمَيْهَا وَ ابْتَدَأَتْ مِنْ أَوَّلِ الشَّمْعِ إِلَى أَنْ أَوْقَدَتِ الثَّمَانِينَ شَمْعَةً ثُمَّ قَعَدَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-nahaḍat ʿalā qadamayhā wa-ibtadaʾat min awwali al-shamʿi ilā an awqadati al-thamānīna shamʿatan thumma qaʿadat
sentences.l: And she rose upon her two feet, and began from the first of-the-candles until she had lit the eighty candles; then she sat.
sentences.i: She rose to her feet and began at the first of the candles, and did not stop until she had lit all eighty. Then she sat down again.
sentences.n: At the end of a printed line the print leaves a lone و before its host word ابتدأت; the two are kept as the print has them. She disobeys the old man's “one candle” on purpose: this is the first stage of her plan. The print gives ابتدأت with the hamza written, so it is kept precomposed.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ نُورُالدِّينِ يَا شَيْخَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَأَنَا أَيْشْ قِسْمِي عِنْدَكَ أَمَا تُخَلِّينِي أُوقِدُ قِنْدِيلًا مِنْ هَذِهِ الْقَنَادِيلِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika qāla Nūru al-Dīni yā shaykha Ibrāhīma wa-anā aysh qismī ʿindaka amā tukhallīnī ūqidu qindīlan min hādhihi al-qanādīli
sentences.l: And after that said Nūr al-Dīn: O shaykh Ibrāhīm, and I — what (is) my portion with you? Will you not let me light a lamp from these lamps?
sentences.i: After that Nūr al-Dīn said, “Shaykh Ibrāhīm, and what is my share with you? Will you not let me light one of these lamps?”
sentences.n: أما تخليني أوقد is the colloquial “won't you let me light?”, with no particle linking the two verbs.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ قُمْ وَأَوْقِدْ قِنْدِيلًا وَاحِدًا وَلَا تَتَثَاقَلْ أَنْتَ الْآخِرُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu qum wa-awqid qindīlan wāḥidan wa-lā tathāqal anta al-ākhiru
sentences.l: And said to him the shaykh Ibrāhīm: Rise and light one lamp, and do not be-sluggish, you, the other.
sentences.i: Shaykh Ibrāhīm said to him, “Up, then, and light a single lamp, and do not hang back — you, too.”
sentences.n: أنت الآخر, “you, the other one”, means “you as well”, set against the girl who has just had her turn. The print writes الآخر with a precomposed madda, which is kept.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ وَابْتَدَأَ مِنْ أَوَّلِهَا إِلَى أَنْ أَوْقَدَ الثَّمَانِينَ قِنْدِيلًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāma wa-ibtadaʾa min awwalihā ilā an awqada al-thamānīna qindīlan
sentences.l: And he rose and began from the first of-them until he lit the eighty lamps.
sentences.i: He got up and began at the first of them, and went on until he had lit all eighty lamps.
sentences.n: The print gives وابتدأ with the hamza written, so it is kept precomposed.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ رَقَصَ الْمَكَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika raqaṣa al-makānu
sentences.l: And at that, danced the place.
sentences.i: And at that the whole place seemed to dance.
sentences.n: “The place danced” is meant of the light: with the lamps and candles all burning, the room dances with brilliance, as well as with the drink.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمَا الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ وَقَدْ غَلَبَ عَلَيْهِ السُّكْرُ أَنْتُمَا أَجْرَعُ مِنِّي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahumā al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu wa-qad ghalaba ʿalayhi al-sukru antumā ajraʿu minnī
sentences.l: And said to-the-two-of-them the shaykh Ibrāhīm, and drunkenness had overcome him: You two (are) more-gulping than I.
sentences.i: The shaykh, now overcome by drink, said to them, “You two can swallow more than I can.”
sentences.n: أجرع is the elative of جرع, “to gulp”, so “better swallowers”, that is, harder drinkers.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ نَهَضَ عَلَى قَدَمَيْهِ وَفَتَحَ الشَّبَابِيكَ جَمِيعًا وَجَلَسَ وَإِيَّا هُمَا يَتَنَادَمُونَ وَيَتَنَاشَدُونَ الْأَشْعَارَ وَقَدْ أَرْهَجَ بِهِمُ الْمَكَانُ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu nahaḍa ʿalā qadamayhi wa-fataḥa al-shabābīka jamīʿan wa-jalasa wa-iyyā humā yatanādamūna wa-yatanāshadūna al-ashʿāra wa-qad arhaja bihimu al-makānu
sentences.l: Then indeed he rose upon his two feet, and opened the windows, all (of them), and sat, and with them (he) — they carouse together and recite to one another the poems; and the place had stirred with them.
sentences.i: Then he rose to his feet, threw open all the windows, and sat down again, and with the two of them he drank, and they recited verses to one another, until the whole place was astir with them.
sentences.n: وايا هما is printed as two words; it is wa-iyyā humā, “and (together) with the two of them”, the old colloquial use of إيّا as a bare preposition. The verb ارهج is rare and I have only its sense from context: the root has to do with stirring up dust, and here, “the place was in a stir”, with noise and light. The open windows matter for what follows: they are what lets the caliph see the light.

sentences.t: فَقَدَّرَ اللَّهُ الْقَادِرُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَجَعَلَ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ لَهُ سَبَبًا أَنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ فِي تِلْكَ السَّاعَةِ تَفَقَّدَ وَنَظَرَ إِلَى الشَّبَابِيكِ الَّتِي فِي نَاحِيَةِ الدِّجْلَةِ فِي ضَوْءِ الْقَمَرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qaddara Allāhu al-qādiru ʿalā kulli shayʾin wa-jaʿala li-kulli shayʾin lahu sababan anna al-khalīfata fī tilka al-sāʿati tafaqqada wa-naẓara ilā al-shabābīki allatī fī nāḥiyati al-Dijlati fī ḍawʾi al-qamari
sentences.l: And God decreed, the Able over every thing, and made for every thing, for it, a cause: that the caliph, in that hour, went-round-inspecting, and looked at the windows which (were) on the side of the Tigris, in the light of the moon.
sentences.i: Now God, who has power over all things, and has set a cause for each, so ordained that at that very hour the caliph was making a round of inspection, and looked toward the windows that gave on the Tigris, in the moonlight.
sentences.n: فقدّر الله … أنّ الخليفة … تفقّد is a long, loose sentence: “God decreed — and made for everything a cause — that the caliph …”. The pointing of the clause is mine: لكل شيء له سببا has له redundantly echoing the preceding لكل شيء. The caliph is Hārūn al-Rashīd. The Tigris is الدجلة here, with the article, as the print has it. تفقّد is “to go round and inspect”, a ruler's night-walk over his palace.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ ضَوْءَ الْقِنْدِيلِ وَالشُّمُوعِ فِى الْبَحْرِ سَاطِعًا
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara ḍawʾa al-qindīli wa-al-shumūʿi fī al-baḥri sāṭiʿan
sentences.l: And he saw the light of-the-lamp and of-the-candles in the sea, shining.
sentences.i: And he saw the light of the lamps and candles shining upon the water.
sentences.n: البحر, “the sea”, is used of the river, whose surface is carrying the reflection. The print has فى with the dotless ى. القنديل is the singular, used for the whole class of lamps.

sentences.t: فَلَاحَتْ مِنَ الْخَلِيفَةِ الْتِفَاتَةٌ فَرَأَى قَصْرَ الْبُسْتَانِ يَرْهَجُ مِنْ تِلْكَ الشُّمُوعِ وَالْقَنَادِيلِ
sentences.tr: fa-lāḥat mina al-khalīfati iltifātatun fa-raʾā qaṣra al-bustāni yarhaju min tilka al-shumūʿi wa-al-qanādīli
sentences.l: And there appeared from the caliph a glance, and he saw the palace of-the-garden stirring from those candles and lamps.
sentences.i: Then, as he chanced to glance aside, he saw the garden palace ablaze with those candles and lamps.
sentences.n: فلاحت منه التفاتة is “a glance occurred to him”. يرهج is the same rare verb as above; here the context says “is aglow, flickering, in a stir”, and I render it so.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ عَلَيَّ بِجَعْفَرٍ الْبَرْ مَكِيِّ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ʿalayya bi-Jaʿfarin al-Bar makiyyi
sentences.l: And he said: On-me (be) Jaʿfar the Barmakid!
sentences.i: He said, “Bring me Jaʿfar the Barmakid!”
sentences.n: The print has the shadda on عليّ, and it is kept. عليّ بـ is the stock command “(let there be) upon me — i.e. bring me — so-and-so”. The print divides البر مكي into two words, which I keep. Jaʿfar al-Barmakī is the caliph's vizier.

sentences.t: فَمَا كَانَ إِلَّاوَقَدْ حَضَرَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ أَمِيرِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-mā kāna illā-wa-qad ḥaḍara bayna yaday amīri al-muʾminīna
sentences.l: And it was not but that he had come into the presence of the Commander of the Faithful.
sentences.i: And it was no time before he stood in the presence of the Commander of the Faithful.
sentences.n: The print joins إلا وقد into one word (الاوقد), which I point as a single word. فما كان إلا وقد is the idiom “it was not long before …”. The print also joins أمير المؤمنين into one word, with the hamza of المؤمنين written, so it is kept precomposed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا كَلْبَ الْوُزَرَاءِ أَتَأْخُذُ مِنِّي مَدِينَةَ بَغْدَادَ وَلَا تُعْلِمُنِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā kalba al-wuzarāʾi a-taʾkhudhu minnī madīnata Baghdāda wa-lā tuʿlimunī
sentences.l: And he said to him: O dog of-the-viziers! Do-you-take from me the city of Baghdad, and do not inform me?
sentences.i: He said to him, “You dog among viziers! Would you take the city of Baghdad from me, and not even tell me?”
sentences.n: The caliph's meaning is “are you taking Baghdad from me without telling me?”; the question runs on in the next unit, where he draws the conclusion.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ جَعْفَرُ أَيْشْ هَذَا الْكَلَامُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu Jaʿfaru aysh hādhā al-kalāmu
sentences.l: And said to him Jaʿfar: What (is) this speech?
sentences.i: Jaʿfar said to him, “What are you saying?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ لَوْلَا أَنَّ مَدِينَةَ بَغْدَادَ أُخِذَتْ مِنِّي مَا كَانَ قَصْرُ التَّمَاثِيلِ يَتَوَقَّدُ بِالْقَنَادِيلِ وَالشُّمُوعِ وَانْفَتَحَتْ شَبَابِيكُهُ وَيْلَكَ مَنِ الَّذِي يَسْتَجْرِي يَفْعَلُ هَذِهِ الْفِعَالَ إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ أَخَذْتَ الْخِلَافَةَ مِنِّي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu law-lā anna madīnata Baghdāda ukhidhat minnī mā kāna qaṣru al-tamāthīli yatawaqqadu bi-al-qanādīli wa-al-shumūʿi wa-infataḥat shabābīkuhu waylaka mani alladhī yastajrī yafʿalu hādhihi al-fiʿāla illā an takūna akhadhta al-khilāfata minnī
sentences.l: And he said to him: Were-it-not that the city of Baghdad was taken from me, the palace of-the-statues would not be kindling with the lamps and the candles, and its windows opened. Woe to-you! Who (is) the one who dares (to) do these deeds, unless you have taken the caliphate from me?
sentences.i: He said to him, “Had the city of Baghdad not been taken from me, the Palace of Statues would not be blazing with lamps and candles, with its windows flung open. Woe to you! Who is it that dares to do such things — unless you have taken the caliphate from me?”
sentences.n: قصر التماثيل, “the Palace of Statues”, is the name of the garden pavilion. The print marks the ت of أخذتَ with a fatḥa, which is kept; it makes the verb plainly “you (m.) have taken”. The sentence is a single outburst: a contrary-to-fact condition (لولا … ما كان), then the second question, then the reproach. يستجري يفعل has two verbs side by side with no linking particle, “dares (and) does”, a colloquial pattern. الفعال is the plural of فعل, “deeds”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ جَعْفَرُ وَقَدِ ارْتَعَدَتْ فَرَائِصُهُ وَمَنْ أَخْبَرَكَ بِأَنَّ قَصْرَ التَّمَاثِيلِ مَوْقُودٌ وَ فُتِحَتْ شَبَابِيكُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Jaʿfaru wa-qadi irtaʿadat farāʾiṣuhu wa-man akhbaraka bi-anna qaṣra al-tamāthīli mawqūdun wa-futiḥat shabābīkuhu
sentences.l: And said Jaʿfar, and his shoulder-muscles had trembled: And who informed you that the palace of-the-statues (is) lit, and its windows opened?
sentences.i: Jaʿfar, whose limbs were trembling, said, “And who told you that the Palace of Statues is lit and its windows open?”
sentences.n: The farāʾiṣ are the muscles at the shoulder or side that quiver with fear; to say they “trembled” is the standard way of saying that a man was terrified. The print has فرائصه with its hamza written, so it is kept precomposed. Here too a lone و is printed at the end of a line, apart from its host فتحت, and is kept apart.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ تَقَدَّمْ عِنْدِي وَانْظُرْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu taqaddam ʿindī wa-unẓur
sentences.l: And he said to him: Come-forward to me, and look.
sentences.i: He said to him, “Come here, to my side, and look.”

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمَ جَعْفَرُ عِنْدَ الْخَلِيفَةِ وَنَظَرْنَا حِيَةَ الْبُسْتَانِ فَوَجَدَ الْقَصْرَ يَشْتَعِلُ بِالْمَصَابِيحِ فِي حِنْدِسِ الظَّلَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddama Jaʿfaru ʿinda al-khalīfati wa-naẓarnā ḥiyata al-bustāni fa-wajada al-qaṣra yashtaʿilu bi-al-maṣābīḥi fī ḥindisi al-ẓalāmi
sentences.l: And Jaʿfar came-forward to the caliph, and looked towards the garden, and found the palace kindling with the lamps in the pitch-darkness of the dark.
sentences.i: So Jaʿfar went forward to the caliph's side and looked toward the garden, and there he found the palace aflame with lamps in the blackest depth of the dark.
sentences.n: The words ونظرنا حية are not good Arabic as printed: “and we looked, a snake of the garden” cannot be meant. The sense is plainly وَنَظَرَ نَاحِيَةَ الْبُسْتَانِ, “and he looked toward the garden”, with the ن of the second word fallen back onto the first; I point the letters as the print has them and translate the sense. حندس is “pitch-dark night”; ظلام repeats it for emphasis, and the sentence ends here without the next clause.

sentences.t: فَأَرَادَ جَعْفَرٌ أَنْ يَعْتَذِرَ عَنِ الشَّيْخِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الْخُولِيِّ رُبَّمَا يَكُونُ هَذَا الْأَمْرُ بِإِذْنِهِ لِمَارَأَى فِيهِ مِنَ الْمَصْلَحَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-arāda Jaʿfarun an yaʿtadhira ʿani al-shaykhi Ibrāhīma al-Khūliyyi rubbamā yakūnu hādhā al-amru bi-idhnihi li-mā raʾā fīhi mina al-maṣlaḥati
sentences.l: And Jaʿfar wanted to make-excuse on-behalf-of the shaykh Ibrāhīm the overseer: perhaps this matter is with his permission, for-what he saw in it of the benefit.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar wished to make excuse for Shaykh Ibrāhīm the Overseer, supposing that the affair might well have been done with the caliph's leave, since he saw some advantage in it.
sentences.n: The print joins لمارأى into one word; it is li-mā raʾā, “because of what he saw”. الخولي (al-Khūlī) is the title of a steward or overseer of an estate or garden; here it follows Ibrāhīm's name like a surname. The “permission” Jaʿfar has in mind is his own, given last week and reported in the next sentences.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ كَانَ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ فِى الْجُمْعَةِ الَّتِي مَضَتْ قَالَ لِي يَاسَيِّدِي جَعْفَرُ إِنِّي أَشْتَهِي أَنْ أُفْرِحَ أَوْلَادِي فِي حَيَاةِ أَمِيرِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَحَيَاتِكَ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ وَأَيْشْ تَحْتَاجُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā amīra al-muʾminīna kāna al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu fī al-jumʿati allatī maḍat qāla lī yā sayyidī Jaʿfaru innī ashtahī an ufriḥa awlādī fī ḥayāti amīri al-muʾminīna wa-ḥayātika fa-qultu lahu wa-ayyish taḥtāju
sentences.l: And he said: O commander-of-the-believers, the shaykh Ibrāhīm was, in the week that passed, he said to me: O my-master Jaʿfar, indeed I desire that I-gladden my-children in the life of-the-commander-of-the-believers and your-life. And I said to-him: And what do-you-need?
sentences.i: He said: Commander of the Faithful, last week Shaykh Ibrāhīm said to me, “My lord Jaʿfar, I long to give my children a feast of joy, while the Commander of the Faithful and you are alive.” And I said to him, “And what do you need?”
sentences.n: الجمعة can mean “Friday” as well as “week”; “the week that passed” seems the likelier sense here. كان … قال is a loose way of saying “had said”. أيش (“what?”) is the colloquial contraction of أيّ شيء. أفرح أولادي is “I gladden my children”, the verb being the one used for holding a feast; the occasion is their circumcision, as the next lines say. In the Arabic, “in the life of the Commander of the Faithful and your life” is a courteous formula meaning “while you both live”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِي تَأْخُذُ لِي مَرْسُومًا مِنَ الْخَلِيفَةِ بِأَنِّي أُطَاهِرُ أَوْلَادِي فِى الْقَصْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lī taʾkhudhu lī marsūman mina al-khalīfati bi-annī uṭāhiru awlādī fī al-qaṣri
sentences.l: And he said to me: You-take for-me a decree from the caliph, that I circumcise my-children in the palace.
sentences.i: Then he said to me, “Obtain for me a decree from the caliph, permitting me to circumcise my children in the palace.”
sentences.n: طاهر is “purify” and is the ordinary word for circumcising a boy. تأخذ لي مرسوما is an indicative used as a request, “you take for me a decree”; the English imperative carries the sense. The بأني clause says what the decree is to authorise.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ رُحْ طَاهِرْهُمْ وَأَنَا أَجْتَمِعُ بِالْخَلِيفَةِ وَأُعْلِمُهُ بِذَلِكَ فَرَاحَ مِنْ عِنْدِي عَلَى هَذَا الْحَالِ وَنَسِيتُ أَنْ أُعْلِمَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu ruḥ ṭāhirhum wa-anā ajtamiʿu bi-al-khalīfati wa-uʿlimuhu bi-dhālika fa-rāḥa min ʿindī ʿalā hādhā al-ḥāli wa-nasītu an uʿlimaka
sentences.l: And I said to-him: Go, circumcise-them, and I meet with-the-caliph and inform-him of that. And he went from with-me on this state, and I forgot that I-inform-you.
sentences.i: I said to him, “Go and circumcise them, and I shall meet the caliph and tell him of it.” So he went away from me on that understanding, and I forgot to inform you.
sentences.n: هذا الحال is printed with a masculine demonstrative; حال is feminine in Classical, masculine here. “On this state” means “with matters standing so”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ يَا جَعْفَرُ كَانَ لَكَ عِنْدِي ذَنْبٌ وَاحِدٌ فَصَارَ لَكَ عِنْدِي ذَنْبَانِ لِأَنَّكَ أَخْطَأْتَ مِنْ وَجْهَيْنِ الْوَجْهُ الْأَوَّلُ أَنَّكَ مَا أَعْلَمْتَنِي بِذَلِكَ وَالْوَجْهُ الثَّانِي أَنَّكَ مَا بَلَّغْتَ الشَّيْخَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مَقْصُودَهُ فَإِنَّهُ مَا جَاءَ إِلَيْكَ وَقَالَ لَكَ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ إِلَّا تَعْرِيضًا لِطَلَبِ شَئٍ مِنَ الْمَالِ يَسْتَعِينُ بِهِ فَلَا أَعْطَيْتُهُ شَئاً وَلَا أَعْلَمْتَنِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu yā Jaʿfaru kāna laka ʿindī dhanbun wāḥidun fa-ṣāra laka ʿindī dhanbāni li-annaka akhṭaʾta min wajhayni al-wajhu al-awwalu annaka mā aʿlamtanī bi-dhālika wa-al-wajhu al-thānī annaka mā ballaghta al-shaykha Ibrāhīma maqṣūdahu fa-innahu mā jāʾa ilayka wa-qāla laka hādhā al-kalāma illā taʿrīḍan li-ṭalabi shayʾin mina al-māli yastaʿīnu bihi fa-lā aʿṭaytuhu shayʾan wa-lā aʿlamtanī
sentences.l: And the caliph said: O Jaʿfar, you had with me one fault, and now-became for-you with me two faults, because you erred in two respects: the first respect, that you did not inform me of that; and the second respect, that you did not make-reach the shaykh Ibrāhīm his aim — for he did not come to you and say to you this speech except as-a-hint for the seeking of something of money, by-which he might help-himself; so neither did I give him anything, nor did you inform me.
sentences.i: The caliph said: Jaʿfar, you already had one fault against you with me, and now you have two, for you erred in two ways. First, that you did not tell me of this; and second, that you did not secure for Shaykh Ibrāhīm what he wanted. He would not have come to you and spoken such words except as a hint that he was seeking some money to help himself with; and so I gave him nothing, and you never told me.
sentences.n: The “one fault” Jaʿfar already had is not named in this passage. The print has the final clause as ولا اعلمتني, “nor did you inform me”, with the negative ولا carrying on from فلا أعطيته. تعريضا is a hint or oblique suggestion, here a request for money dressed up as news. In اخطأت the print itself writes the hamza on its alif seat (أ), so I keep it; the initial alif of the word is bare in the print.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ جَعْفَرٌ يَا أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ نَسِيتُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Jaʿfarun yā amīra al-muʾminīna nasītu
sentences.l: And Jaʿfar said: O commander of-the-believers, I forgot.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar said, “Commander of the Faithful, I forgot.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ وَحَقِّ آبَائِي وَأَجْدَادِي مَا أَتِمُّ بَقِيَّةَ لَيْلَتِي إِلَّا عِنْدَهُ فَإِنَّهُ رَجُلٌ صَالِحٌ يَقُومُ بِالْمَشَائِخِ وَالْفُقَرَاءِ وَيُعِزُّهُمْ وَيَكُونُونَ مُجْتَمِعِينَ عِنْدَهُ عَسَى دَعْوَةُ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمْ يَحْصُلُ لَنَابِهَا خَيْرًا فِى الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ وَفِي هَذَا الْأَمْرِ مَصَالِحُ لَهُ بِحُضُورِى عِنْدَهُ وَيَفْرَحُ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu wa-ḥaqqi ābāʾī wa-ajdādī mā atimmu baqiyyata laylatī illā ʿindahu fa-innahu rajulun ṣāliḥun yaqūmu bi-al-mashāʾikhi wa-al-fuqarāʾi wa-yuʿizzuhum wa-yakūnūna mujtamiʿīna ʿindahu ʿasā daʿwatu wāḥidin minhum yaḥṣulu lanā bihā khayran fī al-dunyā wa-al-ākhirati wa-fī hādhā al-amri maṣāliḥu lahu bi-ḥuḍūrī ʿindahu wa-yafraḥu al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu
sentences.l: And the caliph said: By the right of my fathers and my grandfathers, I will not complete the remainder of my night except at-his-place; for he is a man righteous, he attends-to the elders and the poor, and honours them, and they are gathered at-his-place. Perhaps the prayer of one of them will come-to-pass for us by-it, good in the world and the hereafter; and in this matter (are) benefits for him through my presence at-his-place, and the shaykh Ibrāhīm will rejoice.
sentences.i: The caliph said: By the right of my fathers and forefathers, I will spend the rest of my night nowhere but with him! He is a righteous man who tends the elders and the poor and honours them, and they gather at his house. Perhaps the prayer of one of them may bring us good in this world and the next; and there is gain for him in this too, in my being present with him, and Shaykh Ibrāhīm will be glad.
sentences.n: المشائخ is the print's plural of شيخ (Classical مشايخ), with the hamza written on a seat; I keep it as printed, as I do the hamzas of آبائي and الآخرة. يحصل لنا بها is “comes to us through it”; the print runs لنا and بها together as لنابها, which I point as لَنَا بِهَا without a break. عسى is followed here by a noun and a bare verb, “perhaps the prayer of one of them [will] bring…”. The “poor” (الفقراء) are Sufi mendicants as well as the destitute.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ جَعْفَرٌ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَوَقْتُ أَمْسَى وَهُمُ السَّاعَةَ عَلَى فُرُوغٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Jaʿfarun yā amīra al-muʾminīna awaqtu amsā wa-humu al-sāʿata ʿalā furūghin
sentences.l: And Jaʿfar said: O commander of-the-believers, (is it) a time (when) it-has-become-evening? and they, at-this-hour, (are) on finishing.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar said, “Commander of the Faithful, is this a time to go? Evening has come, and by now they are all but finished.”
sentences.n: The first clause is obscure: اوقت امسى is not a standard construction. I read it as أ + وقت, “[is it] a time?”, followed by أمسى, “evening has come”; the sense would be that it is too late to call, and the party is breaking up. If you read it otherwise, the next clause still fits: على فروغ is “at the point of finishing”, and الساعة is “just now, by this hour”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ لَابُدَّ مِنَ الرَّوَاحِ عِنْدَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu lā budda mina al-rawāḥi ʿindahum
sentences.l: And the caliph said: There-is-no escape from the going to them.
sentences.i: The caliph said, “We must go to them; there is no avoiding it.”
sentences.n: لابد is printed as one word. الرواح is the going out (classically in the evening) to a place.

sentences.t: فَسَكَتَ جَعْفَرٌ وَتَحَيَّرَ وَبَقِيَ لَايَدْرِى مَايَفْعَلُ
sentences.tr: fa-sakata Jaʿfarun wa-taḥayyara wa-baqiya lā yadrī mā yafʿalu
sentences.l: And Jaʿfar fell-silent, and was-bewildered, and remained not knowing what he-does.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar fell silent, bewildered, and stood there not knowing what to do.
sentences.n: The print joins لايدري and مايفعل. بقي followed by a verb, “he remained doing”, is a usual way of saying “he was left … ing”.

sentences.t: فَنَهَضَ الْخَلِيفَةُ عَلَى قَدَمَيْهِ وَبَقِيَ جَعْفَرٌ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَمَعَهُمَا مَسْرُورٌ الْخَادِمُ وَمَشَوْا الثَّلَٰثَةُ مُتَنَكِّرِينَ وَنَزَلُوا مِنْ قَصْرِ الْخِلَافَةِ وَجَعَلُوا يَشُقُّونَ فِى الْأَزِقَّاتِ وَهُمْ فِي زِيِّ التُّجَّارِ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلُوا إِلَى بَابِ الْبُسْتَانِ الْمَذْكُورِ
sentences.tr: fa-nahaḍa al-khalīfatu ʿalā qadamayhi wa-baqiya Jaʿfarun bayna yadayhi wa-maʿahumā Masrūrun al-khādimu wa-mashaw al-thalāthatu mutanakkirīna wa-nazalū min qaṣri al-khilāfati wa-jaʿalū yashuqqūna fī al-aziqqāti wa-hum fī ziyyi al-tujjāri ilā an waṣalū ilā bābi al-bustāni al-madhkūri
sentences.l: And the caliph rose onto his-two-feet, and Jaʿfar stayed between his-two-hands, and with-the-two-of-them (was) Masrūr the servant; and the three walked disguised, and descended from the palace of-the-caliphate, and began cleaving through the alleys, and they in the dress of the merchants, until they arrived at the gate of the garden, the mentioned.
sentences.i: The caliph rose to his feet, with Jaʿfar standing before him and Masrūr the servant beside them, and the three set off in disguise. They went down from the caliph's palace and began to make their way through the alleys in the dress of merchants, until they came to the gate of the garden we have spoken of.
sentences.n: الثلثة is printed without the alif of ثلاثة; I keep it with the dagger alif, as on the previous nights, and as with الثلثون. ومعهما is “with the two of them”, a dual, although three are walking: the two are the caliph and Jaʿfar, and Masrūr is named after them. Masrūr is the caliph's attendant; he is called simply الخادم, “the servant”. بين يديه (“between his two hands”) means “in front of him, in attendance”. الأزقات is the print's plural of زقاق, “alley”. يشقون is “cleave, cut through” the lanes.

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمَ الْخَلِيفَةُ فَرَأَى بَابَ الْبُسْتَانِ مَفْتُوحًا فَتَعَجَّبَ وَقَٰلَ انْظُرْ يَا جَعْفَرُ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ كَيْفَ خَلَّى الْبَابَ مَفْتُوحًا إِلَى هَذَا الْوَقْتِ وَمَا هِيَ عَادَتُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddama al-khalīfatu fa-raʾā bāba al-bustāni maftūḥan fa-taʿajjaba wa-qāla unẓur yā Jaʿfaru al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu kayfa khallā al-bāba maftūḥan ilā hādhā al-waqti wa-mā hiya ʿādatuhu
sentences.l: And the caliph went-forward and saw the gate of-the-garden open, and was-amazed, and said: Look, O Jaʿfar: the shaykh Ibrāhīm — how has he left the door open until this time, and it is not his custom.
sentences.i: The caliph stepped forward and saw the garden gate standing open. Amazed, he said, “Look, Jaʿfar: how has Shaykh Ibrāhīm left the door open at this hour? It is not his habit.”
sentences.n: وقل is the print's spelling of وقال; the dagger alif restores the long ā. The sentence about Ibrāhīm is a dislocated subject, “Shaykh Ibrāhīm — how has he left…”. ما هي عادته is “it is not his custom”, with a feminine pronoun هي agreeing with the unstated “this”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ دَخَلُوا إِلَى أَنْ انْتَهَوْا إِلَى آخِرِ الْبُسْتَانِ وَوَقَفُوا تَحْتَ الْقَصْرِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahum dakhalū ilā an intahaw ilā ākhiri al-bustāni wa-waqafū taḥta al-qaṣri
sentences.l: Then indeed they entered, until they reached the end of-the-garden, and stood beneath the pavilion.
sentences.i: Then they went in, and walked on until they came to the far end of the garden, and stopped beneath the pavilion.
sentences.n: القصر is “palace”, but in a garden it is the lodge or pavilion where the party is held; I translate “pavilion”. The print has آخر with the madda written on the alif, which I keep.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ يَا جَعْفَرُ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَتَسَلَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ قَبْلَ أَنْ أَطْلَعَ لَهُمْ حَتَّى أَنْظُرَ أَيَّ شَيْءٍ هُمْ فِيهِ وَأَنْظُرَ إِلَى الْمَشَائِخِ فَإِنِّي إِلَى الْآنَ لَمْ أَسْمَعْ لَهُمْ حِسًّا وَلَا فَقِيرًا يَذْكُرُ اللَّهَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu yā Jaʿfaru urīdu an atasallala ʿalayhim qabla an aṭlaʿa lahum ḥattā anẓura ayya shayʾin hum fīhi wa-anẓura ilā al-mashāʾikhi fa-innī ilā al-āna lam asmaʿ lahum ḥissan wa-lā faqīran yadhkuru Allāha
sentences.l: And the caliph said: O Jaʿfar, I want to slip upon them before I go-up to them, so-that I may see what thing they (are) in it, and see the elders; for indeed I, until now, have not heard from them a sound, nor a poor-man remembering God.
sentences.i: The caliph said: Jaʿfar, I want to creep up on them before I go up to them, so that I may see what they are about, and look at the shaykhs; for up to now I have not heard a sound from them, nor any dervish invoking God.
sentences.n: أتسلل عليهم is “slip in on them unawares”. أي شيء هم فيه is “what it is that they are in”, that is, what they are doing. فقيرا يذكر الله, “a poor man remembering God”, means a Sufi at his dhikr, the chanted remembrance of God; the caliph hears none of it. The print gives الآن with the madda written, which I keep.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ نَظَرَ فَرَأَى شَجَرَةَ جَوْزٍ عَالِيَةً فَقَالَ يَا جَعْفَرُأُ رِيدُ أَنْ أَطْلَعَ عَلَى هَذِهِ الشَّجَرَةِ فَإِنَّ فُرُوعَهَا قَرِيبَةٌ مِنَ الشُّبَا بِيكِ وَأَنْظُرَ إِلَيْهِمْ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-khalīfata naẓara fa-raʾā shajarata jawzin ʿāliyatan fa-qāla yā Jaʿfaru urīdu an aṭlaʿa ʿalā hādhihi al-shajarati fa-inna furūʿahā qarībatun mina al-shubābīki wa-anẓura ilayhim
sentences.l: Then indeed the caliph looked and saw a tree of-walnut, tall, and said: O Jaʿfar, I want to go-up this tree, for its branches (are) near to the windows, and to see them.
sentences.i: Then the caliph looked about and saw a tall walnut tree. “Jaʿfar,” he said, “I want to climb this tree, for its branches are close to the windows, and I can look in on them.”
sentences.n: The print runs يا جعفرا ريد together with a gap in the wrong place: the alif of أريد has been attached to جعفر, and what is left is ريد. I vocalise the stray alif as أُ so that the two pieces read yā Jaʿfaru urīdu. Likewise الشبا بيك is the print's split of الشبابيك, “the windows”. وأنظر إليهم continues the construction after أن: “… and to see them”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ طَلَعَ فَوْقَ الشَّجَرَةِ وَلَمْ يَزَلْ يَتَعَلَّقُ مِنْ فَرْعٍ إِلَى فَرْعٍ إِلَى أَنْ طَلَعَ عَلَى الْفَرْعِ الَّذِي يُقَابِلُ الشَّبَّاكَ وَقَعَدَ فَوْقَهُ وَنَظَرَ مِنْ شُبَّاكِ الْقَصْرِ فَرَأَى صَبِيَّةً وَصَبِيًّا كَأَنَّهُمَا قَمَرَانِ سُبْحَانَ مَنْ خَلَقَهُمَا وَصَوَّرَ هُمَا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-khalīfata ṭalaʿa fawqa al-shajarati wa-lam yazal yataʿallaqu min farʿin ilā farʿin ilā an ṭalaʿa ʿalā al-farʿi alladhī yuqābilu al-shabbāka wa-qaʿada fawqahu wa-naẓara min shubbāki al-qaṣri fa-raʾā ṣabiyyatan wa-ṣabiyyan ka-annahumā qamarāni subḥāna man khalaqahumā wa-ṣawwara humā
sentences.l: Then indeed the caliph went-up above the tree, and did not cease clinging from branch to branch, until he went-up onto the branch that faces the window, and sat upon it, and looked from the window of-the-pavilion, and saw a girl and a youth, as-if-the-two-of-them (were) two moons. Glory to him who created them and formed them!
sentences.i: Then the caliph climbed into the tree, working his way from branch to branch until he reached the branch that faced the window, and sat on it and looked in through the pavilion window. He saw a girl and a young man, like two moons. Glory to Him who created them and shaped them!
sentences.n: The two young people are, evidently, Anīs al-Jalīs and Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī, the pair whose story this is, though the caliph does not know them. The print has a shadda on the ب of الشباك (the first time), which I keep. قمران, “two moons”, is the standard comparison of beautiful lovers. The print splits وصوّر هما into two words, with a shadda on the و, which I keep.

sentences.t: وَرَأَى الشَّيْخَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ قَاعِدًا وَفِي يَدِهِ قَدَحٌ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ يَا سِتَّ الْمِلَاحِ الشُّرْبُ بِلَا طَرَبٍ مَا هُوَ فَلَاحٌ فَإِنِّي سَمِعْتُ الشَّاعِرَ يَقُولُ شِعْرًا
sentences.tr: wa-raʾā al-shaykha Ibrāhīma qāʿidan wa-fī yadihi qadaḥun wa-huwa yaqūlu yā sitta al-milāḥi al-shurbu bi-lā ṭarabin mā huwa falāḥun fa-innī samiʿtu al-shāʿira yaqūlu shiʿran
sentences.l: And he saw the shaykh Ibrāhīm sitting, and in his hand a cup, and he saying: O lady of-the-fair-ones, the drinking without delight is not success; for indeed I heard the poet say verse:
sentences.i: And he saw Shaykh Ibrāhīm sitting with a cup in his hand, saying, “O mistress of the fair, drinking without music is no good; for I have heard the poet say:”
sentences.n: ست is the colloquial sitt, “lady”, a shortening of سيدة; ست الملاح, “lady of the fair ones”, is a compliment to the girl. طرب is delight, especially the delight of music and song, and فلاح is success or well-being. The poet's verse follows. In the English I take شعرا as introducing it, “verse”.

sentences.t:
آدِرْهَا بِالْكَبِيرِ وَبِالصَّغِيرِ * وَخُذْهَا مِنْ يَدِ الْقَمَرِ الْمُنِيرِ
وَلَا تَشْرَبْ بِلَاطَرَبٍ فَانِي * رَايْتُ الْخَيْلَ تَشْرَبُ بِالصَّفِيرِ
sentences.tr:
ādirhā bi-al-kabīri wa-bi-al-ṣaghīri * wa-khudhhā min yadi al-qamari al-munīri
wa-lā tashrab bi-lā ṭarabin fa-innī * raʾaytu al-khayla tashrabu bi-al-ṣafīri
sentences.l:
Pass-it-round to the great and to the small, * and take it from the hand of-the-moon, the shining;
and do not drink without delight, for I * have seen the horses drink with the whistle.
sentences.i: Pass it round to old and young alike, * and take it from the hand of the shining moon; and never drink without music, for I * have seen the horses drink to the whistle.
sentences.n: Verse, copied as pointed in the print; every word is marked there, so nothing is added. The print writes فَانِي and رَايْتُ with a bare alif, no hamza, and بِلَاطَرَبٍ as one word; I leave them as printed (read fa-innī, raʾaytu, bi-lā ṭarabin). Horses were whistled at while they drank; the poet's joke is that even they will not drink without a tune. آدِرْهَا, “pass it round”, is the host's call to the cup-bearer, and the “cup” is understood.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَايَنَ الْخَلِيفَةُ مِنَ الشَّيْخِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ هَذِهِ الْفِعَالَ قَامَ عِرْقُ الْغَضَبِ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ وَنَزَلَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿāyana al-khalīfatu mina al-shaykhi Ibrāhīma hādhihi al-fiʿāla qāma ʿirqu al-ghaḍabi bayna ʿaynayhi wa-nazala
sentences.l: And when the caliph beheld, from the Shaykh Ibrāhīm, these deeds, rose the vein of-the-anger between his-two-eyes, and he-came-down.
sentences.i: When the caliph saw these doings of Shaykh Ibrāhīm, the vein of wrath swelled between his eyes, and he climbed down.
sentences.n: قام عرق الغضب, literally “the vein of anger rose up”, is an idiom for a throbbing temple: the caliph is furious. From what follows, he and Jaʿfar have been watching from a tree, so نزل means he climbed down from it.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ يَا جَعْفَرُ أَنَا مَا رَأَيْتُ الصَّالِحِينَ عَلَى هَذَا الْحَالِ أَبَدًا فَاطْلَعْ أَنْتَ الْآخَرُ عَلَى هَذِهِ الشَّجَرَةِ وَانْظُرْ لِئَلَّا تَفُوتَكَ بَرَكَاتُ الصَّالِحِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla yā Jaʿfaru anā mā raʾaytu al-ṣāliḥīna ʿalā hādhā al-ḥāli abadan fa-iṭlaʿ anta al-ākhara ʿalā hādhihi al-shajarati wa-unẓur li-allā tafūtaka barakātu al-ṣāliḥīna
sentences.l: And he said: O Jaʿfar, I — I have not seen the righteous upon this state ever; so go-up, you, the other-one, upon this tree, and look, lest escape-you the blessings of-the-righteous.
sentences.i: He said, “Jaʿfar, never have I seen the righteous in such a state! Climb this tree yourself as well, and look, lest the blessings of the righteous pass you by.”
sentences.n: The caliph speaks in bitter irony: “the righteous” is the drinking shaykh, and “the blessings of the righteous” is the show he is about to put on. الآخر after أنت means “you too, in your turn”. هذا الحال treats ḥāl as masculine, which Classical usage allows but does not require.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ جَعْفَرٌ كَلَامَ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ صَارَ مُتَحَيِّرًا فِي أَمْرِهِ وَصَعِدَ إِلَى أَعْلَا الشَّجَرَةِ وَإِذَا بِهِ نَظَرَ فَرَأَى نُورَ الدِّينِ وَالشَّيْخَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَالْجَارِيَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Jaʿfarun kalāma amīri al-muʾminīna ṣāra mutaḥayyiran fī amrihi wa-ṣaʿida ilā aʿlā al-shajarati wa-idhā bihi naẓara fa-raʾā Nūra al-Dīni wa-al-shaykha Ibrāhīma wa-al-jāriyata
sentences.l: And when Jaʿfar heard the speech of the commander of the believers, he became bewildered in his affair, and went-up to the top of-the-tree; and behold, he looked, and saw Nūr al-Dīn and the shaykh Ibrāhīm and the slave-girl.
sentences.i: When Jaʿfar heard the words of the Commander of the Faithful, he was left bewildered as to what to do. He climbed to the top of the tree, and there, as he looked, he saw Nūr al-Dīn, Shaykh Ibrāhīm and the girl.
sentences.n: اعلا is the print's spelling of أعلى, “the top of”. After وإذا the بِـ in به only marks what comes into view; the sense is “and behold, he looked”.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ فِي يَدِهِ الْقَدَحُ فَلَمَّا عَايَنَ جَعْفَرٌ تِلْكَ الْحَالَةَ أَيْقَنَ بِالْهَلَاكِ وَنَزَلُو وَقَفَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu fī yadihi al-qadaḥu fa-lammā ʿāyana Jaʿfarun tilka al-ḥālata ayqana bi-al-halāki wa-nazalū waqafa bayna yaday amīri al-muʾminīna
sentences.l: And the shaykh Ibrāhīm — in his hand the cup. And when Jaʿfar beheld that state, he was-certain of destruction, and came-down (ū), stood between the two-hands of the commander of the believers.
sentences.i: Shaykh Ibrāhīm had the cup in his hand, and when Jaʿfar saw the scene he was certain he was doomed. He climbed down and stood before the Commander of the Faithful.
sentences.n: The print has ونزلو with a stray final و: the sense is “he came down” and then “stood”, with the two verbs simply side by side. I vocalise the letters as printed. بين يدي, “between the two hands of”, means “in the presence of”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْخَلِيفَةُ يَا جَعْفَرُ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي جَعَلَنَا مِنَ الْمُتَّبِعِينَ لِظَاهِرِ الشَّرِيعَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-khalīfatu yā Jaʿfaru al-ḥamdu li-Allāhi alladhī jaʿalanā mina al-muttabiʿīna li-ẓāhiri al-sharīʿati
sentences.l: And the caliph said to him: O Jaʿfar, the praise (is) to God who made us among the followers of the outward of-the-law.
sentences.i: The caliph said to him, “Jaʿfar, praise be to God, who has made us of those who hold to the outward form of the Law!”
sentences.n: The caliph's praise is sarcasm: he and Jaʿfar keep only the “outside” (ظاهر) of the sharia, while the shaykh before them is doing something quite different.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَقْدِرْ جَعْفَرٌ يَتَكَلَّمُ مِنْ شِدَّةِ الْخَجَلِ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yaqdir Jaʿfarun yatakallamu min shiddati al-khajali
sentences.l: And Jaʿfar was not able to speak, from the intensity of-the-shame.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar could not speak, so great was his shame.
sentences.n: يقدر يتكلم has no أن between the verbs, as is usual in Middle Arabic; the second verb stands in the indicative, with no subjunctive marker. Watch for this construction.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَظَرَ الْخَلِيفَةُ إِلَى جَعْفَرٍ وَقَالَ يَا تَرِي مَنْ أَوْصَلَ هَؤُلَاءِ إِلَى هَذَا الْمَكَانِ وَمَنْ أَدْخَلَهُمْ قَصْرِي وَلَكِنْ مِثْلَ حُسْنِ هَذَا الصَّبِيِّ وَهَذِهِ الصَّبِيَّةِ مَا رَأَتْ عَيْنِى قَطُّ
sentences.tr: thumma naẓara al-khalīfatu ilā Jaʿfarin wa-qāla yā tarā man awṣala hāʾulāʾi ilā hādhā al-makāni wa-man adkhalahum qaṣrī wa-lākin mithla ḥusni hādhā al-ṣabiyyi wa-hādhihi al-ṣabiyyati mā raʾat ʿaynī qaṭṭu
sentences.l: Then the caliph looked at Jaʿfar and said: O you-see — who conveyed these to this place, and who made-them-enter my palace? But the like of the beauty of this lad and this lass, has not seen my eye ever.
sentences.i: Then the caliph looked at Jaʿfar and said, “I wonder who brought these people to this place, and who let them into my palace! Yet the like of the beauty of this youth and this girl my eyes have never seen.”
sentences.n: يا ترى, literally “O, you see”, is a set phrase meaning “I wonder”. The caliph is baffled, since the garden is his own and he has not yet taken in who these people are. The print has رأت with a precomposed hamza, which is kept; مثل is fronted as the object of the verb, for emphasis. عين is feminine, hence the feminine verb.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ جَعْفَرُوَقَدِ اسْتَرْجَى رِضَاءَ الْخَلِيفَةِ هَرُونَ الرَّشِيدِ صَدَقْتَ يَا مَوْلَانَا السُّلْطَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Jaʿfaruwa-qadi istarjā riḍāʾa al-khalīfati Hārūna al-Rashīdi ṣadaqta yā mawlānā al-sulṭānu
sentences.l: And Jaʿfar said — and he had hoped-for the contentment of the caliph Hārūn al-Rashīd — You have spoken truly, O our lord the sultan.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar, hoping to win back the favour of the caliph Hārūn al-Rashīd, answered, “You have spoken truly, my lord the sultan.”
sentences.n: The print runs جعفر and وقد together; I vocalise them as Jaʿfaru wa-qadi. استرجى is obscure to me: the sense required is “he sought, hoped for”, but I cannot name the form with certainty. رضاء is the print's spelling of رضا. Calling the caliph “sultan” is a Middle Arabic habit; the text uses the two titles freely for him.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا جَعْفَرُ اطْلَعْ بِنَا إِلَى هَذَا الْفَرْعِ الَّذِى هُوَ مُقَابِلُهُمْ لِنَتَفَرَّجَ عَلَيْهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā Jaʿfaru iṭlaʿ bi-nā ilā hādhā al-farʿi alladhī huwa muqābiluhum li-natafarraja ʿalayhim
sentences.l: And he said: O Jaʿfar, go-up with-us to this branch which it (is) facing-them, that-we-may-take-our-ease upon them.
sentences.i: Then he said, “Jaʿfar, let us climb to that bough facing them, that we may watch them at our ease.”
sentences.n: اطلع بنا, “go up with us”, is an invitation to climb together. تفرج على is “to look on at leisure, to be entertained by”. The relative clause الذي هو مقابلهم repeats the pronoun هو, which Classical would leave out; a common Middle Arabic feature.

sentences.t: فَطَلَعَ الْاِثْنَانِ عَلَى الشَّجَرَةِ وَنَظَرَا هُمَا فَسَمِعَا الشَّيْخَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ يَقُولُ يَا سَادَتِي قَدْ تَرَكْتُ الْوَقَارَ بِشُرْبِ الْعُقَارِ وَلَايَلَذُّ ذَلِكَ إِلَّابِنَغَمَاتِ الْأَوْتَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṭalaʿa al-ithnāni ʿalā al-shajarati wa-naẓarā humā fa-samiʿā al-shaykha Ibrāhīma yaqūlu yā sādatī qad taraktu al-waqāra bi-shurbi al-ʿuqāri wa-lā yaladhdhu dhālika illā bi-naghamāti al-awtāri
sentences.l: And the two went-up upon the tree, and looked — the-two-of-them — and heard Shaykh Ibrāhīm saying: O my masters, I have left the dignity through the drinking of-the-wine, and that is not sweet except with the melodies of-the-strings.
sentences.i: The two of them climbed into the tree and looked, and heard Shaykh Ibrāhīm saying, “My masters, I have cast off dignity by drinking wine, and wine is sweet only with the notes of strings.”
sentences.n: The print writes ونظرا هما as two words; I read “and they looked at the two of them” (the clitic هما split off from نظرا), though “they looked, the two of them” is also possible. ولايلذ and إلابنغمات are printed as run-together words. The clauses rhyme: الوقار، العقار، الأوتار. العقار is wine.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ أَنِيسُ الْجَلِيسِ يَا شَيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ وَاللَّهِ لَوْ كَانَ عِنْدَنَا شَيْءٌ مِنْ آلَاتِ الطَّرَبِ لَكَانَ مُرُورُنَا كَامِلًا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu Anīsu al-Jalīsi yā shaykhu Ibrāhīmu wa-Allāhi law kāna ʿindanā shayʾun min ālāti al-ṭarabi la-kāna mururunā kāmilan
sentences.l: And Anīs al-Jalīs said to him: O shaykh Ibrāhīm, by God, if there were with us anything of the instruments of-the-music, our delight (printed: “our passing”) would be complete.
sentences.i: Anīs al-Jalīs said to him, “Shaykh Ibrāhīm, by God, if only we had some instrument of music here, our delight would be complete.”
sentences.n: The print has مرورنا, “our passing”, which gives no sense here; it is almost certainly a slip for سرورنا, “our delight”, and I translate accordingly while vocalising the letters as printed. Anīs al-Jalīs is the girl's name, “Companion of the Companion” in effect. الطرب is joy in music, and آلات الطرب are musical instruments. The print has آلات and شيء with their own marks, kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ كَلَامَ الْجَارِيَةِ نَهَضَ قَائِمًا عَلَى قَدَمَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu kalāma al-jāriyati nahaḍa qāʾiman ʿalā qadamayhi
sentences.l: And when Shaykh Ibrāhīm heard the speech of-the-slave-girl, he rose, standing, upon his-two-feet.
sentences.i: When Shaykh Ibrāhīm heard the girl's words, he sprang to his feet.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ لِجَعْفَرٍ يَا تَرَى أَيْشِ رَائِحٌ يَعْمَلُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu li-Jaʿfarin yā tarā ayshi rāʾiḥun yaʿmalu
sentences.l: And the caliph said to Jaʿfar: I-wonder — what (is) going he-does?
sentences.i: The caliph said to Jaʿfar, “I wonder what he is going to do.”
sentences.n: ايش is colloquial for أي شيء, “what?”, and رائح followed by an imperfect verb is the colloquial future, “is going to do”. This is spoken Arabic breaking through the page. The print has a precomposed ئ in رائح, kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ جَعْفَرٌ لَا أَدْرِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Jaʿfarun lā adrī
sentences.l: And Jaʿfar said: I do not know.

sentences.t: فَغَابَ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ وَعَادَ وَمَعَهُ عُودٌ فَتَأَمَّلَهُ الْخَلِيفَةُ فَإِذَا هُوَ عُودُ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ النَّدِيمِ
sentences.tr: fa-ghāba al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu wa-ʿāda wa-maʿahu ʿūdun fa-taʾammalahu al-khalīfatu fa-idhā huwa ʿūdu Abī Isḥāqa al-Nadīmi
sentences.l: And Shaykh Ibrāhīm went-away and returned, and with him a lute; and the caliph examined it, and behold, it (was) the lute of Abū Isḥāq the boon-companion.
sentences.i: Shaykh Ibrāhīm slipped away and came back with a lute. The caliph looked it over, and behold, it was the lute of Abū Isḥāq the boon-companion.
sentences.n: Abū Isḥāq al-Nadīm, “the boon-companion”, is evidently one of the caliph's own court musicians, so the caliph recognises an instrument from his own household; the story does not stop to explain. A عود is the Arabic lute.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ وَاللَّهِ إِنْ غَنَّتْ هَذِهِ الْجَارِيَةُ وَحْشًا لَأَصْلُبَنَّكُمْ كُلَّكُمْ وَإِنْ غَنَّتْ مَلِيحًا فَإِنِّي عَفَوْتُ عَنْهُمْ وَأَصْلُبُكَ أَنْتَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu wa-Allāhi in ghannat hādhihi al-jāriyatu waḥshan la-aṣlubannakum kullakum wa-in ghannat malīḥan fa-innī ʿafawtu ʿanhum wa-aṣlubuka anta
sentences.l: And the caliph said: By God, if this slave-girl sings ugly, I will-surely-crucify you, all-of-you; and if she sings fine, then I have pardoned them, and I will-crucify you, you.
sentences.i: The caliph said, “By God, if this girl sings badly I will crucify the lot of you; and if she sings well, I will pardon them, and crucify you alone.”
sentences.n: وحشا is “ugly, coarse” (literally “wild”), the opposite of مليحا, “fine, pleasing”. The caliph speaks in a jest that carries a real threat; the “you” of the first clause is Jaʿfar and the garden party, the “them” the offenders he is willing to pardon, and the “you” of the last clause is Jaʿfar alone. The perfect after إن is the usual conditional “if she sings”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ جَعْفَرٌ اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْهَا تُغَنِّي وَحْشًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Jaʿfarun Allāhumma ijʿalhā tughannī waḥshan
sentences.l: And Jaʿfar said: O God, make her sing ugly.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar said, “O God, make her sing badly!”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ لِأَيِّ شَيْءٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu li-ayyi shayʾin
sentences.l: And the caliph said: for what thing?
sentences.i: The caliph said, “Why so?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ تَصْلُبَنَا كُلَّنَا نُؤْنِسُ بَعْضُنَا الْبَعْضَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla li-ajli an taṣlubanā kullanā nuʾnisu baʿḍunā al-baʿḍa
sentences.l: And he said: for the sake that you crucify us, all-of-us, we keep-company, some-of-us the some.
sentences.i: He said, “So that, when you crucify us all, we may keep one another company.”
sentences.n: Jaʿfar's gallows joke has two clauses set side by side with no conjunction: “that you crucify us all — we keep each other company”. بعضنا البعض is “each other” with the article added on the second word, as often in later Arabic. The print has نؤنس with its own ؤ.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ الْخَلِيفَةُ مِنْ كَلَامِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika al-khalīfatu min kalāmihi
sentences.l: And the caliph laughed at his speech.
sentences.i: The caliph laughed at his words.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْجَارِيَةَ أَخَذَتِ الْعُودَ وَافْتَقَدَتْهُ وَأَصْلَحَتْ أَوْ تَارَهُ وَضَرَبَتْ ضَرْبًا فَتَشَوَّقَتِ الْقُلُوبُ إِلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-jāriyata akhadhati al-ʿūda wa-iftaqadathu wa-aṣlaḥat aw tārahu wa-ḍarabat ḍarban fa-tashawwaqati al-qulūbu ilayhā
sentences.l: Then indeed the slave-girl took the lute, and inspected it, and set-right its strings, and struck a striking, and the hearts yearned toward her.
sentences.i: Then the girl took up the lute and looked it over, tuned its strings, and played a prelude, and every heart was stirred with longing toward her.
sentences.n: The print splits أوتاره (“its strings”) into أو تاره across a space: I keep the two pieces as printed and read them as one word. افتقد here means “to examine, to test”. ضربت ضربا, literally “she struck a striking”, is the usual way of saying that a musician played.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنْشَدَتْ وَجَعَلَتْ تَقُولُ شِعْ—رًا
sentences.tr: thumma anshadat wa-jaʿalat taqūlu shiʿ—ran
sentences.l: Then she recited, and she set-about saying, verse:
sentences.i: Then she began to recite these verses:
sentences.n: The print breaks شعرا with a dash, شع—را, and the dash is kept; the word is شعرًا, “as verse”.

sentences.t:
يَا نَاصِرِينَ مَسَاكِينَا مُحِبِّينَا * نَارُ الْمَحَبَّةِ وَ الْاَشْوَاقِ تَكْوِينَا
مَهْمَا فَعَلْتُمْ فَكُنَّا مُسْتَحِقِّينَا * نَحْنُ اسْجُرْنَا بِكُمْ لَا تَشْمُتُوا فِينَا
فَاِنَّنَا اَهْلُ ذُلٍّ ثُمَّ مَسْكَنَةٍ * مَهْمَا تَشَاءُوهُ فَهَذَا فَافْعَلُوا فِينَا
مَا الْفَخْرُ اَنْ تَقْتُلُوْنَا فِي مَنَازِلِكُمْ * وَاِنَّمَا خَوْفُنَا اَنْ تَا ثَمُوا فِينَا
sentences.tr:
yā nāṣirīna masākīnanā muḥibbīnā * nāru al-maḥabbati wa-al-ashwāqi takwīnā
mahmā faʿaltum fa-kunnā mustaḥiqqīnā * naḥnu usjurnā bikum lā tashmutū fīnā
fa-innanā ahlu dhullin thumma maskanatin * mahmā tashāʾūhu fa-hādhā fa-afʿalū fīnā
mā al-fakhru an taqtulūnā fī manāzilikum * wa-innamā khawfunā an taʾthamū fīnā
sentences.l:
O helpers — poor-ones-of-ours, lovers-of-ours — * the fire of-the-love and of-the-longings brands-us.
Whatever you do — so we were deserving — * we, we are set-ablaze by-you; do not gloat over-us.
For indeed we (are) people of abasement, then of-wretchedness; * whatever you wish of-it — this — so do (it) to-us.
Not (is) the boast that you kill-us in your dwellings, * but our fear (is) that you incur-sin concerning-us.
sentences.i:
O you who aid us, poor wretches and your lovers, * the fire of love and longing sears us.
Whatever you do, we deserve it; * we are ablaze because of you, so do not gloat over us.
For we are people of abasement and then of misery: * whatever you desire, do it to us.
It is no glory to kill us in your own dwellings; * what we fear is that you will bring sin upon yourselves through us.
sentences.n: Verse, copied as pointed in the print, with its marks and spacing (وَ الْاَشْوَاقِ and تَا ثَمُوا are printed with a space inside them). The grammar is loose for the sake of the rhyme in -īnā: the first hemistich puts مساكينا and محبينا in a row after the vocative, and تكوينا is best read as “it brands us” (from كوى), the long -ā being only the rhyme vowel. اسْجُرْنَا is printed with a damma on the jīm; I take it as “we are set ablaze” (as if اُسْجِرْنَا) and leave it as printed. تَا ثَمُوا is تَأْثَمُوا, “you incur sin”, split by the space.

sentences.t: نَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ وَاللّٰهِ طَيِّبٌ يَا جَعْفَرُ عُمْرِي مَاسَمِعْتُ صَوْتًا مُطْرِبًا مِثْلَ هَذَا
sentences.tr: naqāla al-khalīfatu wa-Allāhi ṭayyibun yā Jaʿfaru ʿumrī mā-samiʿtu ṣawtan muṭriban mithla hādhā
sentences.l: Said the caliph: By-God, good! O Jaʿfar, my-lifetime — I-have-not-heard a voice delighting, the-like-of this.
sentences.i: The caliph said, “By God, Jaʿfar, that is fine! In all my life I have never heard so ravishing a voice as this.”
sentences.n: The print has نقال, with ن where فقال (“and he said”) is plainly meant; I vocalise the letters as they stand and read it as fa-qāla. طيب, “good”, is an exclamation of delight here. عمري ماسمعت, literally “my lifetime — I have not heard”, is the idiom for “never in my life have I heard”; ماسمعت is printed as one word. مطربا is a voice that moves the hearer with ṭarab, delight in song.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ جَعْفَرُ لَعَلَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ ذَهَبَ مَا عِنْدَهُ مِنَ الْغَيْظِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Jaʿfaru laʿalla al-khalīfata dhahaba mā ʿindahu mina al-ghayẓi
sentences.l: And said Jaʿfar: Perhaps the caliph — has-gone what (is) with-him of the rage.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar said, “Perhaps the caliph's anger has left him.”
sentences.n: The construction is loose: الخليفة stands in the accusative after لعل, and a whole clause with its own subject follows (“there has gone what he had of rage”), so the sentence is about the caliph and says what has happened to his temper.

sentences.t: قَالَ نَعَمْ ذَهَبَ
sentences.tr: qāla naʿam dhahaba
sentences.l: He said: Yes, it-has-gone.
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “it has gone.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَزَلَ مِنْ فَوْقِ الشَّجَرَةِ هُوَ وَ جَعْفَرُ ثُمَّ الْتَفَتَ إِلَى جَعْفَرٍ وَ قَالَ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَطْلَعَ وَاجْلِسَ عِنْدَ هُمْ وَاسْمَعَ الصَّبِيَّةَ تُغَنِّي فُدَّامِي
sentences.tr: thumma nazala min fawqi al-shajarati huwa wa Jaʿfaru thumma iltafata ilā Jaʿfarin wa qāla urīdu an aṭlaʿa wa-ajlisa ʿinda hum wa-asmaʿa al-ṣabiyyata tughannī fuddāmī
sentences.l: Then he-came-down from above the tree, he and Jaʿfar; then he-turned to Jaʿfar and said: I-want that I-go-up and sit with them and hear the girl singing in-front-of-me.
sentences.i: Then he climbed down from the tree, he and Jaʿfar, and turned to Jaʿfar and said, “I want to go up and sit with them, and to hear the girl sing before me.”
sentences.n: The print has ف where قدامي (colloquial qudāmī, “in front of me”) is meant, and spaces the words هو و جعفر and عند هم apart; I keep the printing and vocalise the letters as they stand. The last three verbs (أطلع، أجلس، أسمع) are subjunctive after أن with the wāw of the later two carrying the series. الصبية is the young girl, the singer of the garden. طلع, “go up”, is the verb for entering the pavilion from the garden.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذَا طَلَعْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ رُبَّمَــا تَكَدَّرُوا وَأَمَّا الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ فَيَمُـــوتُ مِنَ الْخَوْفِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā amīra al-muʾminīna idhā ṭalaʿta ʿalayhim rubbamā takaddarū wa-ammā al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu fa-yamūtu mina al-khawfi
sentences.l: And he said: O commander of-the-believers, if you-go-up upon them, perhaps they-will-be-clouded; and as-for the shaykh Ibrāhīm, he-will-die from the fear.
sentences.i: He said, “Commander of the Faithful, if you go up to them they may be put out of humour; and as for Shaykh Ibrāhīm, he will die of fright.”
sentences.n: تكدروا lacks the final nūn that a Classical subjunctive plural would have kept, and the print stretches ربما and فيموت with kashida strokes; both are kept as printed. تكدر, “be clouded, disturbed”, is said of a mood or a pleasure spoiled. The speaker is Jaʿfar; الشيخ إبراهيم is the keeper of the garden. In the print the hamza of المؤمنين is on its wāw seat, so it is kept precomposed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ يَا جَعْفَرُ لَا بُدَّ أَنْ تُعَرِّفَنِي أَنْ أَتَحَيَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِحِيلَةٍ وَأَدْخُلَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ غَيْرِأَنْ يَشْعُرُ وابِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu yā Jaʿfaru lā budda an tuʿarrifanī an ataḥayyala ʿalayhim bi-ḥīlatin wa-adkhula ʿalayhim min ghayri-an yashʿuru wābī
sentences.l: And said the caliph: O Jaʿfar, there-is-no escape that you make-me-know (how) that I contrive upon them with a ruse and enter upon them from without-that they-perceive me.
sentences.i: The caliph said, “Jaʿfar, you must tell me how I may devise some stratagem against them and come in upon them without their noticing me.”
sentences.n: I read تعرفني as the causative تُعَرِّفَنِي, “you must let me know”, with the thing to be known (how to contrive) implied; the Classical construction would have a complement such as كيف. غيران is glued غير + أن, “without that”. The print splits يشعروا بي into يشعر وابي; I vocalise it as one word broken across the space, يَشْعُرُ + وا بِي, “they notice me”, with the plural ending carried over into the next token.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ وَجَعْفَرَ ذَهَبَا إِلَى نَاحِيَةِ الدِّجْلَةِ وَ هُمَا مُتَفَكِّرَانِ فِى هَذَا الْأَمْرِ وَإِذَا بِصَيَّادٍ وَ اقِفٍ يَصْطَادُ تَحْتَ شَبَابِيكِ الْقَصْرِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-khalīfata wa-Jaʿfara dhahabā ilā nāḥiyati al-Dijlati wa humā mutafakkirāni fī hādhā al-amri wa-idhā bi-ṣayyādin wa āqifin yaṣṭādu taḥta shabābīki al-qaṣri
sentences.l: Then indeed the caliph and Jaʿfar went to the side of-the-Tigris, and they-two (were) thinking-it-over about this matter, and behold, a fisherman standing, fishing beneath the windows of-the-palace.
sentences.i: Then the caliph and Jaʿfar made their way toward the bank of the Tigris, turning this matter over between them; and behold, a fisherman stood there fishing beneath the palace windows.
sentences.n: The print gives جعفر with no alif for the accusative after إن, and spells واقف as two words و اقف; both are kept, and I give the name a bare fatḥa. الدجلة is the Tigris with the article. إذا بـ introduces a sudden sight: “and behold …”.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْخَلِيفَةُ سَابِقًا زَعَقَ عَلَى الشَّيْخِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَقَالَ لَهُ مَا هَذَا الْحِسُّ الَّذِي سَمِعْتُهُ تَحْتَ شَبَابِيكِ الْقَصْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-khalīfatu sābiqan zaʿaqa ʿalā al-shaykhi Ibrāhīma wa-qāla lahu mā hādhā al-ḥissu alladhī samiʿtuhu taḥta shabābīki al-qaṣri
sentences.l: And the caliph had been formerly (one who) shouted at the shaykh Ibrāhīm and said to him: What (is) this noise that I-heard beneath the windows of-the-palace?
sentences.i: Now the caliph had earlier shouted at Shaykh Ibrāhīm, saying, “What is this noise I heard beneath the palace windows?”
sentences.n: وكان … زعق is a pluperfect, “had shouted”: the narrator steps back to explain why the river bank under the palace is empty. سابقا is “formerly, earlier”. زعق على is “to shout at”, a colloquial verb. الحس is “sound, stir of voices”. The relative الذي is followed by a pronoun object (سمعته) that Classical Arabic would also keep.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ صَوْتُ صَيَّادِينَ السَّمَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu ṣawtu ṣayyādīna al-samaki
sentences.l: And said to-him the shaykh Ibrāhīm: The voice of-fishermen of-the-fish.
sentences.i: Shaykh Ibrāhīm said to him, “It is the voice of the fishermen.”
sentences.n: Classical would drop the nūn of a sound plural in an iḍāfa (صيادو السمك, صيادي السمك); the print keeps it, صَيَّادِينَ السَّمَكِ, “fish-catchers”, and so do I.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ انْزِلْ وَامْنَعْهُمْ مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْمَوْضِعِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla inzil wa-imnaʿhum min dhālika al-mawḍiʿi
sentences.l: And he said: Go-down and prevent them from that place.
sentences.i: “Go down,” said the caliph, “and keep them away from that spot.”

sentences.t: فَامْتَنَعَتِ الصَّيَّادُونَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْمَوْضِعِ
sentences.tr: fa-imtanaʿati al-ṣayyādūna min dhālika al-mawḍiʿi
sentences.l: And refrained-she the fishermen from that place.
sentences.i: So the fishermen kept away from that place.
sentences.n: The verb is feminine singular (امتنعت) with a masculine plural subject, as the print has it; Classical would use امتنعوا, but this agreement is common in Middle Arabic.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتْ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةُ جَاءَ صَيَّادُ سَمَكٍ يُسَمَّى كَرِيمًا وَرَأَى بَابَ الْبُسْتَانِ مَفْتُوحًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānat tilka al-laylatu jāʾa ṣayyādu samakin yusammā Karīman wa-raʾā bāba al-bustāni maftūḥan
sentences.l: And when that night was, there-came a fisherman of-fish, named Karīm, and he-saw the door of-the-garden open.
sentences.i: When that night came, a fisherman named Karīm arrived, and saw the garden gate standing open.
sentences.n: فلما كانت … is the ordinary “when it was that night”; the fisherman is a different man from the crowd that was driven off. كريم is a common name, “Generous”. رأى is printed with a plain alif (راى), so the hamza is ours.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ هَذَا وَقْتُ غَفْلَةٍ اِغْتَنِمْ فِي هَذَا الْوَقْتِ صَيْدَ السَّمَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla fī nafsihi hādhā waqtu ghaflatin ightanim fī hādhā al-waqti ṣayda al-samaki
sentences.l: And he said in himself: This (is) a time of-heedlessness; seize in this time the catching of-fish.
sentences.i: He said to himself, “This is a moment of heedlessness; seize the hour and fish.”
sentences.n: اغتنم can be read as the imperative اِغْتَنِمْ, “seize!”, a man talking himself into it, or as the first-person أَغْتَنِمُ, “I shall seize”. I take the imperative; the sense is almost the same. غفلة is the heedlessness of the guards and the keeper.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخَذَ شَبَكَتَهُ وَ طَرَحَهَا فِى الْبَحْرِ وَإِذَا بِالْخَلِيفَةِ وَحْدَهُ وَ اقِفَ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma akhadha shabakatahu wa ṭaraḥahā fī al-baḥri wa-idhā bi-al-khalīfati waḥdahu wa āqifa ʿalā raʾsihi
sentences.l: Then he-took his-net and cast-it into the sea, and behold, the caliph, alone, standing over his head.
sentences.i: Then he took his net and cast it into the river; and behold, there stood the caliph, alone, over him.
sentences.n: البحر, “the sea”, is the river here (the Tigris); Arabic uses it for any great water. After إذا بـ the print gives واقف as a bare word split in two; I give it a fatḥa, as a circumstantial accusative (“standing”), since there is no alif for the tanwīn. على رأسه is “at his head”, that is, right beside him.

sentences.t: فَعَرَفَهُ الْخَلِيفَةُ فَقَالَ لَهُ يَاكَرِيمُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿarafahu al-khalīfatu fa-qāla lahu yā-karīmu
sentences.l: And the caliph knew him, and said to-him: O-Karīm!
sentences.i: The caliph recognised him and called to him, “Karīm!”
sentences.n: ياكريم is printed as one word. كريم is both a personal name and the common adjective “generous”.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَ إِلَيْهِ لَمَّا سَمِعَهُ يُسَمِّيهِ بِا سْمِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-iltafata ilayhi lammā samiʿahu yusammīhi bi-a smihi
sentences.l: And he-turned to him when he-heard him naming him by-his-name.
sentences.i: He turned toward him when he heard himself called by name.
sentences.n: The print splits باسمه into با سمه; I keep the two tokens and vocalise the first as بِا (bi-, the preposition, plus the alif of ism) and the second as سْمِهِ. The subject of التفت is the fisherman; the speaker is the caliph.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى الْخَلِيفَةَ ارْتَعَدَتْ فَرَائِصُهُ وَقَالَ وَاللّٰهِ يَا أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ مَا فَعَلْتُهُ اسْتِهْزَاءً بِالْمَرْسُومِ وَلَٰكِنِ الْفَقْرُ وَالْعَيْلَةُ قَدْ حَمَلَانِي عَلَى مَا تَرَى
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā al-khalīfata irtaʿadat farāʾiṣuhu wa-qāla wa-Allāhi yā amīra al-muʾminīna mā faʿaltuhu istihzāʾan bi-al-marsūmi wa-lākini al-faqru wa-al-ʿaylatu qad ḥamalānī ʿalā mā tarā
sentences.l: And when he-saw the caliph, trembled his-flanks, and he-said: By-God, O commander of-the-believers, I-did-not-do-it in-mockery of-the-decree, but poverty and want have-carried me upon what you-see.
sentences.i: When he saw the caliph, his flesh trembled, and he said, “By God, Commander of the Faithful, I did not do this to flout the decree. It is poverty and want that have driven me to what you see.”
sentences.n: The print gives فرائصه with a precomposed hamza, kept as printed; الفرائص are the muscles of the flank that quiver in fear, so ارتعدت فرائصه is the stock phrase for a man shaking with dread. المرسوم is the official decree (here, the ban on fishing under the palace). حملاني is correctly dual, as the subject is the two nouns الفقر والعيلة. ولكن is printed without the alif, so it carries a dagger alif.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ اِصْطَلْ عَلَى اسْمِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu iṣṭal ʿalā ismī
sentences.l: And said the caliph: Fish upon my-name.
sentences.i: The caliph said, “Cast your net in my name.”
sentences.n: The print has اصطل, which as printed would be a verb of warming oneself; the sense calls for اصطد (iṣṭad), “fish!”, with ل for د, a misprint or a slip. I vocalise the letters as they stand and translate the sense. على اسمي is “on my account, in my name”, the caliph taking the catch on himself.

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمَ الصَّيَّادُ وَقَدْ فَرِحَ وَطَرَحَ الشَّبَكَةَ وَصَبَرَ حَتَّى أَخَذَتْ حَدَّهَا وَثَبَتَتْ فِى الْقَرَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddama al-ṣayyādu wa-qad fariḥa wa-ṭaraḥa al-shabakata wa-ṣabara ḥattā akhadhat ḥaddahā wa-thabatat fī al-qarāri
sentences.l: And the fisherman advanced, having rejoiced, and cast the net and waited until it-took its limit and settled in the bottom.
sentences.i: The fisherman stepped forward, glad at heart, and cast the net and waited until it had taken its full extent and settled on the bottom.
sentences.n: أخذت حدها is “it took its limit”, the net spreading out as far as its ropes allow; القرار is the bed of the river.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ جَذَبَهَا إِلَيْهِ فَطَلَعَ فِيهَا مِنْ أَنْوَاعِ السَّمَكِ فَفَرِحَ بِذَلِكَ الْخَلِيفَةُ
sentences.tr: thumma jadhabahā ilayhi fa-ṭalaʿa fīhā min anwāʿi al-samaki fa-fariḥa bi-dhālika al-khalīfatu
sentences.l: Then he-drew it to him, and there-came-up in it of kinds of-fish, and the caliph rejoiced at that.
sentences.i: Then he hauled it in toward him, and up in it came fish of every kind; and the caliph was delighted at the sight.
sentences.n: طلع فيها is “there came up in it” (the net), with the subject من أنواع السمك, “some of the kinds of fish”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا كَرِيمُ اقْلَعْ ثِيَابَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā Karīmu iqlaʿ thiyābaka
sentences.l: And he said: O Karīm, take-off your-clothes.
sentences.i: Then he said, “Karīm, take off your clothes.”

sentences.t: فَقَلَعَ ثِيَابَهُ وَكَانَتْ عَلَيْهِ جُبَّةٌ فِيهَا مِائَةُ رُقْعَةٍ مِنَ الصُّوفِ الْخَشِنِ وَفِيهَا مِنَ الْقَمْلِ الْمُذْنِبِ
sentences.tr: fa-qalaʿa thiyābahu wa-kānat ʿalayhi jubbatun fīhā miʾatu ruqʿatin mina al-ṣūfi al-khashini wa-fīhā mina al-qamli al-mudhnibi
sentences.l: And he-took-off his-clothes; and there-was upon him a robe, in-it a hundred patches of the rough wool, and in-it of the lice, the sinful ones.
sentences.i: So he took off his clothes. He had on a woollen gown with a hundred patches of coarse wool sewn into it, and teeming with lice, the wicked things.
sentences.n: المذنب is obscure. As vocalised it is “the offending, the guilty” (مُذْنِب), a jest on the lice as sinners; another candidate is “the long-tailed, the big” (مُذَنَّب). I give the first. The print has مائة with a precomposed hamza, kept as printed. الجبة is the long outer gown of wool.

sentences.t: وَقَلَعَ مِنْ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ عِمَامَةً وَكَانَ لَهَا ثَلَٰثُ سِنِينَ مَا حَلَّهَا إِلَّاكُلَّ مَا رَأَى خِرْقَةً خَيَّطَهَا عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qalaʿa min ʿalā raʾsihi ʿimāmatan wa-kāna lahā thalāthu sinīna mā ḥallahā illā-kulla mā raʾā khirqatan khayyaṭahā ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And he-took-off from upon his head a turban, and there-were to-it three years; he-did-not-untie-it except every-time he-saw a rag he-sewed it upon it.
sentences.i: He pulled off the turban from his head as well. It was three years old, and he had never unwound it, save that whenever he saw a rag he stitched it on.
sentences.n: ثلث is the print's ثلاث with the alif missing, so it carries a dagger alif. إلاكل is printed as one word, إلا كل, “except every”; ما رأى is “whatever he saw”. حلها is “untie it (the turban)”. The sense is that the turban had grown by accretion, never unwound.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَلَعَ الْجُبَّةَ وَالْعِمَامَةَ خَلَعَ الْخَلِيفَةُ مِنْ فَوْقِ جِسْمِهِ ثَوْبَيْنِ سَكَنْدَرِيٍّ وَبَعْلَبَكِّيٍّ مِنْ حَرِيرٍ وَمَلُوطَةً وَفَرَجِيَّةً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qalaʿa al-jubbata wa-al-ʿimāmata khalaʿa al-khalīfatu min fawqi jismihi thawbayni sakandariyyin wa-baʿlabakkiyyin min ḥarīrin wa-malūṭatan wa-farajiyyatan
sentences.l: And when he-took-off the robe and the turban, the caliph stripped from above his-body two garments, an-Alexandrian and a-Baalbeki, of silk, and a cloak and a long-coat.
sentences.i: When the fisherman had taken off the gown and the turban, the caliph stripped from his body two silk garments, one of Alexandria and one of Baalbek, together with a malūṭa cloak and a farajiyya coat.
sentences.n: The print has سكندري without the alif of إسكندري, the usual Middle Arabic form; the two garments are named for their places of weaving, Alexandria and Baalbek.
