I read ملوطة and فرجية as two further objects of خلع, “a malūṭa and a farajiyya”: a malūṭa is a kind of outer cloak and a farajiyya a long robe with wide sleeves. The print does not make clear that these are items beyond the pair of garments, so the division is mine.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لِلصَّيَّادِ خُذْهُمْ وَالْبَسْهُمْ وَلَبِسَ الْخَلِيفَةُ جُبَّةَ الصَّيَّادِ وَعِمَامَتَهُ وَضَرَبَ لَهُ لِثَامَ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla li-al-ṣayyādi khudhhum wa-ilbashum wa-labisa al-khalīfatu jubbata al-ṣayyādi wa-ʿimāmatahu wa-ḍaraba lahu lithāma
sentences.l: Then he said to-the-fisherman: Take them and put-them-on; and the caliph put-on the fisherman's robe and his-turban, and struck for-himself a face-veil.
sentences.i: Then he said to the fisherman, “Take these and put them on.” And the caliph put on the fisherman's gown and turban and wrapped a veil about his face.
sentences.n: The print has لثام without an alif for the accusative; I give it a bare fatḥa. ضرب له لثام is “he fastened a veil on himself”, the له reflexive (the caliph's own face). The lithām covers the lower face, nose and mouth, and here completes the disguise.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لِلصَّيَّادِ رُحْ أَنْتَ إِلَى شُغْلِكَ فَقَبَّلَ رِجْلَ الْخَلِيفَةِ وَشَكَرَهُ وَجَعَلَ يَقُولُ شِعْ — رًا
sentences.tr: thumma qāla li-al-ṣayyādi ruḥ anta ilā shughlika fa-qabbala rijla al-khalīfati wa-shakarahu wa-jaʿala yaqūlu shiʿ — ran
sentences.l: Then he said to-the-fisherman: Go, you, to your-work. And he-kissed the foot of-the-caliph and thanked him and began saying poetry.
sentences.i: Then he said to the fisherman, “Be off, you, about your business.” And the man kissed the caliph's foot and thanked him, and began to recite these lines:
sentences.n: The word شعرا is broken across a line in the print (شع — را); I keep the break and the dash, and vocalise it as shiʿran, “(in) verse”. رح is the colloquial imperative “go off”; انت adds emphasis, “you, go!”.

sentences.t:
اَوْ لَيْتَنِي نُعْمَى ابُوحُ بِشُكْرِهَا * وَكَفَيْتَنِي كُلَّ الْاُمُورِ بِاَسْرِهَا
فَلَا شَكَرْتَنَّكَ مَا حَيِيتُ وَإِنْ امُتْ * شَكَرْتُكَ مِنِّي اعْظُمِي فِي قَبْرِهَا
sentences.tr:
aw laytanī nuʿmā abūḥu bi-shukrihā * wa-kafaytanī kulla al-umūri bi-asrihā
fa-lā shakartanna-ka mā ḥayītu wa-in amut * shakartuka minnī aʿẓumī fī qabrihā
sentences.l:
Or would-that-me a-favour, I-declare with-its-thanks, * and you-have-spared-me all the affairs in-their-entirety;
then-not I-thanked-surely-you as-long-as I-live, and if I-die * have-thanked-you from me my-bones in its-grave.
sentences.i: Would that I had some boon whose thanks I might proclaim, * and you had spared me all my troubles, every one. I shall thank you as long as I live; and if I die, * my very bones will thank you in their grave.
sentences.n: Verse, copied as pointed in the print, so nothing is added; the marks that look odd are the print's (a plain alif with fatḥa in اَوْ and اَسْرِهَا, and the damma-marked ابُوحُ and امُتْ). The first couplet is hard: اَوْ لَيْتَنِي (“or would that I …”) is followed by a past verb, وَكَفَيْتَنِي, and I give the loose sense, that the fisherman wishes he could repay the generosity. فَلَا شَكَرْتَنَّكَ is printed with a second-person ending (-ta) and the energetic nūn; the sense demands فلأشكرنك, “I shall surely thank you”, and I translate that. The feminine pronoun in قَبْرِهَا has no clear antecedent; I take it as the bones' own grave (“their grave”). شَكَرْتُكَ has a first-person ending although its subject is “my bones” (اعظمي); I read the clause as “from me, my bones in their grave have thanked you”.

sentences.t: فَمَا فَرَغَ الصَّيَّادُ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ حَتَّى دَبَّ الْقَمْلُ عَلَى جِلْدِ الْخَلِيفَةِ فَصَارَ يَقْبِضُ بِيَدِهِ الْيَمِينِ وَالشِّمَالِ مِنْ عَلَى رَقَبَتِهِ وَيَرْمِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-mā faragha al-ṣayyādu min shiʿrihi ḥattā dabba al-qamlu ʿalā jildi al-khalīfati fa-ṣāra yaqbiḍu bi-yadihi al-yamīni wa-al-shimāli min ʿalā raqabatihi wa-yarmīhi
sentences.l: And the fisherman had-not finished with his-poetry until the lice crept upon the skin of-the-caliph; and he-began seizing with his-hand, the right and the left, from upon his-neck, and throwing it.
sentences.i: The fisherman had scarcely finished his verses when the lice began to creep over the caliph's skin, and he took to snatching at them on his neck, with his right hand and his left, and flinging them away.
sentences.n: فما … حتى is “no sooner … than”. القمل is a collective noun, so the pronoun in يرميه is a singular “it”, which I give as “them”. بيده اليمين والشمال is “with his hand, the right and the left”: the two adjectives follow the one noun, a loose way of saying “with each hand in turn”. من على رقبته is “from off his neck”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ يَا صَيَّادُ وَيْلَكَ مَا هَذَا إِلَّا قَمْلٌ كَثِيرٌ فِي هَذِهِ الْجُبَّةِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla yā ṣayyādu waylaka mā hādhā illā qamlun kathīrun fī hādhihi al-jubbati
sentences.l: Then he said: O fisherman, woe-to-you! This (is) nothing but much lice in this robe.
sentences.i: Then he said, “Fisherman, curse you! There is nothing in this gown but lice, and plenty of them.”
sentences.n: ويلك, “woe to you”, is an oath of exasperation rather than a real curse. Note the adjective كثير, “much”, with the plural-sense noun قمل, “lice”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدِي هَذِهِ السَّاعَةَ يُؤْلِمُكَ فَإِذَا مَضَتْ عَلَيْكَ جُمْعَةٌ لَا تُحِسُّ بِهِ وَلَا تُفَكِّرُ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā sayyidī hādhihi al-sāʿata yuʾlimuka fa-idhā maḍat ʿalayka jumʿatun lā tuḥissu bihi wa-lā tufakkiru fīhi
sentences.l: And he said: O my-master, this hour it-pains-you; and when a week has-passed upon you, you-will-not-feel it, and will-not think about it.
sentences.i: He said, “My lord, it pains you now; but when a week has passed over you, you will neither feel it nor give it a thought.”
sentences.n: The print has a precomposed hamza in يؤلمك, which is kept. هذه الساعة is “this hour, now”, an adverbial accusative. جمعة is “a week”, from the sense of “gathering” of seven days. The pronouns in به and فيه refer back to the lice.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ الْخَلِيفَةُ وَقَالَ لَهُ وَيْلَكَ أَنَا أُخَلِّي هَذِهِ الْجُبَّةَ عَلَى جَسَدِي
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika al-khalīfatu wa-qāla lahu waylaka ana ukhallī hādhihi al-jubbata ʿalā jasadī
sentences.l: And the caliph laughed and said to-him: Woe-to-you! I — I-leave this robe upon my-body!
sentences.i: The caliph laughed and said, “Curse you! Am I to leave this gown on my body?”
sentences.n: The sentence can be read as a question or an exclamation of dismay; the Arabic gives no sign. أخلي is the colloquial “I leave, keep”, from خلّى.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الصَّيَّادُ إِنِّي أَشْتَهِي أَقُولُ لَكَ كَلَامًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ṣayyādu innī ashtahī aqūlu laka kalāman
sentences.l: And the fisherman said: Indeed I desire I-say to-you a word.
sentences.i: The fisherman said, “There is something I should like to say to you.”
sentences.n: اشتهي أقول, “I wish I say”, has no أن between the two verbs, which is usual in Middle Arabic and colloquial speech.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ قُلْ مَا عِنْدَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu qul mā ʿindaka
sentences.l: And he said to-him: Say what (is) with-you.
sentences.i: “Say what you have to say,” the caliph answered.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ خَطَرَ بِبَالِي يَا أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ لَمَّا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَتَعَلَّمَ الصَّيْدَ لِأَ جْلِ مَا يَبْقَى فِي يَدِكَ صَنْعَةٌ تَنْفَعُكَ فَيُنَا سِبُكَ هَذِهِ الْجُبَّةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu khaṭara bi-bālī yā amīra al-muʾminīna lammā aradta an tataʿallama al-ṣayda li-a jli mā yabqā fī yadika ṣanʿatun tanfaʿuka fa-yunā sibuka hādhihi al-jubbatu
sentences.l: And he said to-him: It-passed by my-mind, O commander of-the-believers, when you-wished that you-learn the fishing, for the-sake-of what remains in your-hand a craft that-profits-you, then suits-you this robe.
sentences.i: He said, “It came to my mind, Commander of the Faithful, that when you wished to learn fishing, so as to have a trade in your hand to profit you, then this gown would suit you.”
sentences.n: The print splits لأجل into لا جل, and فيناسبك into فينا سبك; I keep the breaks and vocalise the pieces as if one word, لِأَجْلِ and فَيُنَاسِبُكَ (“so it suits you”), the subject being هذه الجبة. ما يبقى is “so that there may remain”, a loose use of ما; Classical would have أن يبقى or حتى يبقى. خطر ببالي is “it crossed my mind”.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ الْخَلِيفَةُ مِنْ كَلَامِ الصَّيَّادِ ثُمَّ وَلَّى الصَّيَّادُ إِلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika al-khalīfatu min kalāmi al-ṣayyādi thumma wallā al-ṣayyādu ilā ḥāli sabīlihi
sentences.l: And laughed the caliph at the speech of-the-fisherman; then turned the fisherman to the state of-his-way.
sentences.i: The caliph laughed at the fisherman's words, and the fisherman went off upon his way.
sentences.n: حال سبيله, literally "the state of his road", is an idiom for "went about his business".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ أَخَذَ مِقْطَفَ السَّمَكِ وَوَضَعَ فَوْقَهُ قَلِيلًا مِنَ الْخُضْرَةِ وَأَتَى بِهِ إِى جَعْفَرٍ وَوَقَفَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-khalīfata akhadha miqṭafa al-samaki wa-waḍaʿa fawqahu qalīlan mina al-khuḍrati wa-atā bihi ilā Jaʿfarin wa-waqafa bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: Then indeed the caliph took the basket of-the-fish, and put over it a little of the greenery, and came with-it to Jaʿfar, and stood between his-two-hands.
sentences.i: Then the caliph took up the fisherman's fish-basket, laid a little greenery over it, carried it to Jaʿfar, and stood before him.
sentences.n: The print has اى for الى (the lām has dropped out); I point it إِى and read it as ilā, "to". بين يديه, "between his two hands", is the ordinary way of saying "in front of him". The greenery covers the fish and keeps the disguise up.

sentences.t: فَاعْتَقَدَ جَعْفَرٌ أَنَّهُ كَرِيمٌ الصَّيَّادُ فَخَافَ عَلَيْهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَاكَرِيمُ أَيْشْ جَاءَ بِكَ هُنَا اِنْجُ بِنَفْسِكَ فَإِنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةَ فِى الْبُسْتَانِ وَمَتَى رَأَكَ رَاحَتْ رَقَبَتُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-iʿtaqada Jaʿfarun annahu Karīmun al-ṣayyādu fa-khāfa ʿalayhi wa-qāla lahu yā-Karīmu aysh jāʾa bika hunā unjū bi-nafsika fa-inna al-khalīfata hādhihi al-laylata fī al-bustāni wa-matā raʾāka rāḥat raqabatuka
sentences.l: And believed Jaʿfar that-he (was) Karīm the fisherman, and feared for him, and said to him: O Karīm, what brought you here? Save yourself! For the caliph, this night, (is) in the garden, and when he sees you, goes your neck.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar took him for Karīm the fisherman and feared for him. "Karīm," he said, "what brings you here? Save yourself! The caliph is in the garden tonight, and if he sets eyes on you, your head is gone."
sentences.n: ايش is the colloquial "what?" (a contraction of أي شيء), and you will meet it often. راحت رقبتك, "your neck has gone", is a blunt way of saying "you will be beheaded". The print gives رأك with a precomposed hamza, which is kept.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْخَلِيفَةُ كَلَامَ جَعْفَرٍ ضَحِكَ فَلَمَّا ضَحِكَ عَرَفَهُ جَعْفَرٌ فَقَالَ لَهُ لَعَلَّكَ مَوْلَانَا السُّلْطَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-khalīfatu kalāma Jaʿfarin ḍaḥika fa-lammā ḍaḥika ʿarafahu Jaʿfarun fa-qāla lahu laʿallaka mawlānā al-sulṭānu
sentences.l: And when heard the caliph the speech of-Jaʿfar, he laughed; and when he laughed, Jaʿfar knew him, and said to him: Perhaps-you (are) our lord the sultan.
sentences.i: When the caliph heard Jaʿfar's words he laughed, and at his laughter Jaʿfar knew him, and said, "Can it be you, our lord the sultan?"
sentences.n: Jaʿfar calls his master "the sultan" rather than "Commander of the Faithful", perhaps because there are others about in the garden. لعلك with a noun after it is read here as "can it be that you are ...?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ نَعَمْ يَاجَعْفَرُ وَأَنْتَ وَزِيرِي وَجِئْتُ أَنَا وَإِيَّاكَ هُنَا وَمَا عَرَفْتَنِي فَكَيْفَ يَعْرِفُنِي الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ وَهُوَ سَكْرَانُ فَكُنْ مَكَانَكَ حَتَّى أَرْجِعَ إِلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu naʿam yā-Jaʿfaru wa-anta wazīrī wa-jiʾtu anā wa-iyyāka hunā wa-mā ʿarafatanī fa-kayfa yaʿrifunī al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu wa-huwa sakrānu fa-kun makānaka ḥattā arjiʿa ilayka
sentences.l: And the caliph said: Yes, O Jaʿfar — and you (are) my vizier, and I came, I and you, here, and you did not know me; so how would know me the shaykh Ibrāhīm, and he (is) drunk? So be (in) your place until I return to you.
sentences.i: "Yes, Jaʿfar," said the caliph. "You are my vizier, you and I came here together, and still you did not know me. How then should Shaykh Ibrāhīm know me, drunk as he is? Stay where you are until I come back to you."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ جَعْفَرٌ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Jaʿfarun samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: And Jaʿfar said: Hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar answered, "With hearing and obedience."
sentences.n: The formula is printed as bare accusatives, "[I give] hearing and obedience"; the usual بالسمع والطاعة has the same sense.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ تَقَدَّمَ إِلَى بَابِ الْقَصْرِ وَطَرَقَهُ طَرْقًا خَفِيفًا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-khalīfata taqaddama ilā bābi al-qaṣri wa-ṭaraqahu ṭarqan khafīfan
sentences.l: Then indeed the caliph advanced to the door of-the-palace and knocked-it a light knocking.
sentences.i: Then the caliph went up to the palace door and knocked on it softly.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ نُورُ الدِّينِ يَاشَيْخَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بَابُ الْقَصْرِ يُدَقُّ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Nūru al-Dīni yā-shaykha Ibrāhīma bābu al-qaṣri yudaqqu
sentences.l: And Nūr al-Dīn said: O shaykh Ibrāhīm, the door of-the-palace is-knocked.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn said, "Shaykh Ibrāhīm, someone is knocking at the palace door."
sentences.n: Here and below the print joins يا to the following word (ياشيخ, ياكريم, ياجعفر); I keep that and show the vocative in the transliteration with a hyphen.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ مَنْ بِالْبَابِ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَنَا يَاشَيْخَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فَقَالَ لَهُ مَنْ أَنْتَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu man bi-al-bābi fa-qāla lahu anā yā-shaykha Ibrāhīma fa-qāla lahu man anta
sentences.l: And the shaykh Ibrāhīm said: Who (is) at-the-door? And he said to him: I, O shaykh Ibrāhīm. And he said to him: Who are-you?
sentences.i: "Who is at the door?" asked Shaykh Ibrāhīm. "It is I, Shaykh Ibrāhīm," came the answer. "And who are you?" he asked.

sentences.t: قَالَ أَنَا كَرِيمٌ الصَّيَّادُ وَسَمِعْتُ أَنَّ عِنْدَكَ أَضْيَافًا فَجِئْتُ إِلَيْكَ بِشَيٌ مِنَ السَّمَكِ فَإِنَّهُ مَلِيحٌ
sentences.tr: qāla anā Karīmun al-ṣayyādu wa-samiʿtu anna ʿindaka aḍyāfan fa-jiʾtu ilayka bi-shayʾin mina al-samaki fa-innahu malīḥun
sentences.l: He said: I (am) Karīm the fisherman, and I heard that with-you (are) guests, so I came to-you with something of the fish, for it (is) fine.
sentences.i: "I am Karīm the fisherman," he said. "I heard that you have guests, so I have come to you with some fish, and fine fish it is."
sentences.n: The print marks the ي of شيٌ with a tanwīn damma, as if for شيءٍ; I keep the mark and read bi-shayʾin, "with something". The ئ of فجئت is the print's own, and is kept precomposed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ نُورُ الدِّينِ سِيرَةَ السَّمَكِ فَرِحَ هُوَ وَجَارِيَتُهُ وَقَالَا يَاسَيِّدِي اِفْتَحْ لَهُ وَدَعْهُ يَدْخُلْ لَنَا بِالسَّمَكِ الَّذِي مَعَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Nūru al-Dīni sīrata al-samaki fariḥa huwa wa-jāriyatuhu wa-qālā yā-sayyidī iftaḥ lahu wa-daʿhu yadkhul lanā bi-al-samaki alladhī maʿahu
sentences.l: And when heard Nūr al-Dīn the mention of-the-fish, he rejoiced, he and his slave-girl, and the-two said: O my master, open to-him, and leave-him (that) he-enter for-us with-the-fish which (is) with-him.
sentences.i: When Nūr al-Dīn heard talk of fish, he and his girl rejoiced, and they said, "Master, open to him, and let him come in to us with the fish he has."
sentences.n: سيرة السمك is literally "the tale of the fish", here simply "the mention of fish". قالا is dual, "the two of them said": Nūr al-Dīn and the girl speak together to Ibrāhīm.

sentences.t: فَفَتَحَ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ الْبَابَ فَدَخَلَ الْخَلِيفَةُ وَهُوَ فِي صُورَةِ الصَّيَّادِ وَابْتَدَأَ بِالسَّلَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-fataḥa al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu al-bāba fa-dakhala al-khalīfatu wa-huwa fī ṣūrati al-ṣayyādi wa-ibtadaʾa bi-al-salāmi
sentences.l: And opened the shaykh Ibrāhīm the door, and entered the caliph, and he (was) in the form of-the-fisherman, and began with-the-greeting.
sentences.i: Shaykh Ibrāhīm opened the door, and the caliph entered in the guise of the fisherman, and began with a greeting.
sentences.n: ابتدأ بـ is "begin with": the verb takes its object with بـ, which is why بالسلام is explained that way in the glossary. The print's final أ is precomposed and kept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ أَهْلًا بِاللِّصِّ السَّارِقِ الْمُقَا مِرْتَعَالَ أَرْنَا السَّمَكَ الَّذِي مَعَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu ahlan bi-al-liṣṣi al-sāriqi al-muqā mirtaʿāla arnā al-samaka alladhī maʿaka
sentences.l: And said to him the shaykh Ibrāhīm: Welcome to-the thief, the robber, the gambler — come! Show-us the fish which (is) with-you.
sentences.i: Shaykh Ibrāhīm said to him, "Welcome to the thief, the robber, the gambler! Come, show us the fish you have."
sentences.n: The line-break has cut a word: المقا is the beginning of المقامر, "the gambler", and its last two letters (مر) are printed attached to تعال, "come!", giving مرتعال. I keep the print's spacing and point the two pieces as they stand. The mock-abuse is a drunk man's banter. Note that the print has a fatḥa on the alif of ارنا, kept.

sentences.t: فَأَرَاهُمْ إِيَّاهُ فَلَمَّا نَظَرُوهُ فَإِذَا هُوَ بِالْحَيَوٰةِ يَتَحَرَّكُ
sentences.tr: fa-arāhum iyyāhu fa-lammā naẓarūhu fa-idhā huwa bi-al-ḥayawati yataḥarraku
sentences.l: And he showed-them it; and when they looked-at-it, behold, it (was) with-the-life, moving.
sentences.i: He showed it to them, and when they looked, behold, it was alive and moving.
sentences.n: The print spells الحيوة with a wāw and no alif; the dagger alif marks the missing long ā (ḥayāh). After فإذا the بـ of بالحيوة only marks what is seen: "behold, it was alive".

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ وَاللَّهِ يَا سَيِّدِي إِنَّ هَذَا السَّمَكَ مَلِيحٌ يَا لَيْتَهُ مَقْلِيٌّ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-jāriyatu wa-Allāhi yā-sayyidī inna hādhā al-samaka malīḥun yā-laytahu maqliyyun
sentences.l: And said the slave-girl: By-God, O my master, indeed this fish (is) fine; O would-that-it (were) fried!
sentences.i: The girl said, "By God, master, this is fine fish. If only it were fried!"
sentences.n: After يا ليته Classical wants the accusative مقليًّا; the print has no alif, so I point the nominative as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ وَاللَّهِ يَاسِتِّي صَدَقْتِ ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ قَالَ لِلْخَلِيفَةِ يَاصَيَّادُ لِأَيْشْ مَا جِئْتَ بِهَذَا السَّمَكِ مَقْلِيًّا قُمِ الْآنَ وَاقْلِهِ لَنَا وَهَاتِهِ لَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu wa-Allāhi yā-sittī ṣadaqti thumma innahu qāla li-al-khalīfati yā-ṣayyādu li-aysh mā jiʾta bi-hādhā al-samaki maqliyyan qumi al-āna wa-aqlihi lanā wa-hātihi lanā
sentences.l: And the shaykh Ibrāhīm said: By-God, O my lady, you-spoke-truly. Then he said to-the-caliph: O fisherman, for-what did-you-not come with this fish fried? Rise now, and fry-it for-us, and bring-it for-us.
sentences.i: Shaykh Ibrāhīm said, "By God, my lady, you have spoken truly." Then he said to the caliph, "Fisherman, why did you not bring this fish already fried? Up with you now; fry it for us and bring it here."
sentences.n: ياستي is colloquial يا ستّي, "my lady". لايش is لـ + ايش, "why?" (literally "for what?"). The kasra on صدقتِ, and the الآن with its precomposed hamza, are the print's own and kept. هات is the colloquial imperative "give, bring".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ حَاضِرْ أَقْلِيهِ لَكُمْ وَأَجِيئُهُ فَقَالُوا لَهُ هَيَّا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu ḥāḍir aqlīhi lakum wa-ajīʾuhu fa-qālū lahu hayyā
sentences.l: And the caliph said: At-hand! I-fry-it for-you and I-bring-it. And they said to him: Come-on!
sentences.i: "At your service," said the caliph. "I shall fry it for you and bring it." "Be quick about it!" they said.
sentences.n: حاضر, "present, ready", is the servant's colloquial "right away". Both verbs are plain presents, "I fry it ... and bring it", with the sense of a promise.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ الْخَلِيفَةُ يَجْرِي حَتَّى وَصَلَ إِلَى جَعْفَرٍ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَاجَعْفَرُ فَقَالَ نَعَمْ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ خَيْرًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāma al-khalīfatu yajrī ḥattā waṣala ilā Jaʿfarin wa-qāla lahu yā-Jaʿfaru fa-qāla naʿam yā-amīra al-muʾminīna khayran
sentences.l: And rose the caliph, running, until he reached Jaʿfar, and said to him: O Jaʿfar. And he said: Yes, O commander of-the-believers — (may it be) good.
sentences.i: The caliph got up and ran until he reached Jaʿfar, and said, "Jaʿfar!" "Yes, Commander of the Faithful," he answered. "May it be for good!"
sentences.n: خيرا, "[may it be] good", is what a man says when summoned unexpectedly and fears bad news. يجري ("running") is a present with no conjunction, describing how he rose.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ طَالَبُوا السَّمَكَ مِنِّي مَقْلِيًّا فَقَالَ جَعْفَرٌ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ هَانَّهُ وَأَنَا أَقْلِيهِ لَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu ṭālabū al-samaka minnī maqliyyan fa-qāla Jaʿfarun yā-amīra al-muʾminīna hānnahu wa-anā aqlīhi lahum
sentences.l: And he said to him: They have demanded the fish of me fried. And Jaʿfar said: O commander of-the-believers, here-indeed-it — and I will-fry-it for-them.
sentences.i: "They have asked me for the fish fried," said the caliph. "Commander of the Faithful," said Jaʿfar, "here it is, and I shall fry it for them."
sentences.n: هانه is obscure. I read it as ها + إنه, "lo, it ...", with the alif lost, and translate "here it is"; the sense, "let me do it", is clear from what follows.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ وَتُرْبَةِ آبَائِي وَأَجْدَادِي مَا يَقْلِيهِ إِلَّا أَنَا بِيَدِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu wa-turbati ābāʾī wa-ajdādī mā yaqlīhi illā anā bi-yadī
sentences.l: And the caliph said: And by-the-grave of-my-fathers and my-grandfathers, none fries-it except I, with-my-hand.
sentences.i: The caliph said, "By the grave of my fathers and forefathers, none shall fry it but I, with my own hand!"
sentences.n: The wāw of وتربة is the wāw of oath, as in واللَّه. The آ and ئ in آبائي are the print's own, and kept precomposed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ أَتَى إِلَى خُصِّ الْخُونِيِّ وَفَتَّشَ فِيهِ فَوَجَدَ كُلَّ مَا يَحْتَاجُهُ فِيهِ حَتَّى الْمِلْحَ وَالزَّعْفَرَانَ وَالصَّعْتَرَ وَغَيْرَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-khalīfata atā ilā khuṣṣi al-khūniyyi wa-fattasha fīhi fa-wajada kulla mā yaḥtājuhu fīhi ḥattā al-milḥa wa-al-zaʿfarāna wa-al-ṣaʿtara wa-ghayra dhālika
sentences.l: Then indeed the caliph came to the hut of-the-khūnī, and searched in it, and found everything that he needs in it, even the salt and the saffron and the thyme and other-than that.
sentences.i: Then the caliph went to the caterer's shed and searched it, and found everything he needed: salt, saffron, thyme, and the rest.
sentences.n: خص is a hut or shed. الخوني is obscure and I vocalise it as a nisba, "the khūnī"; it may belong to خوان, the table on which food is served, so "the table-keeper's shed", which is why I say "caterer's" in the idiomatic layer. Take that as a guess. الصعتر is the colloquial form of الزعتر, thyme.

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمَ الْمَكَانُونَ وَعَلَّقَ الطَّاجِنَ وَقَلَاهُ قَلْيًا مَلِيحًا
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddama al-makānūna wa-ʿallaqa al-ṭājina wa-qalāhu qalyan malīḥan
sentences.l: And he advanced (to) the hearth, and hung the pan, and fried-it a fine frying.
sentences.i: He went up to the hearth, set the pan over it, and fried the fish well.
sentences.n: المكانون is not a word I can place with confidence; it looks like الكانون, "the brazier, hearth", with a stray م, or a form of مكان, and I give it as printed with the sense "hearth". الطاجن is the frying-pan or pot (tājin).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا اسْتَوَى جَعَلَهُ عَلَى وَرَقِ الْمَوْزِ وَأَخَذَ مِنَ الْبُسْتَانِ نَفْيًا وَلِيمُونًا وَطَلَعَ بِالسَّمَكِ وَوَضَعَهُ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā istawā jaʿalahu ʿalā waraqi al-mawzi wa-akhadha mina al-bustāni nafyan wa-līmūnan wa-ṭalaʿa bi-al-samaki wa-waḍaʿahu bayna aydīhim
sentences.l: And when it was-done, he put-it on the leaf of-the-banana, and took from the garden nafy and lemon, and went-up with-the-fish and placed-it between their-hands.
sentences.i: When it was cooked, he laid it on banana leaves, took some nafy and lemons from the garden, and carried the fish up and set it before them.
sentences.n: نفيا is obscure, and I have not found it; since it is gathered from the garden to go with fish, it is an herb or relish, perhaps mint (نعنع) written wrongly. I leave it unglossed in the idiomatic layer as "nafy".

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمَ الصَّبِيُّ وَالصَّبِيَّةُ وَالشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ وَأَكَلُوا فَلَمَّا فَرَغُوا مِنَ الْأَكْلِ غَسَلُوا أَيْدِيَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddama al-ṣabiyyu wa-al-ṣabiyyatu wa-al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu wa-akalū fa-lammā faraghū mina al-akli ghasalū aydiyahum
sentences.l: And advanced the youth and the maiden and the shaykh Ibrāhīm, and they ate; and when they finished from the eating, they washed their-hands.
sentences.i: The young man, the young woman and Shaykh Ibrāhīm drew near and ate, and when they had finished eating they washed their hands.
sentences.n: الصبي والصبية are Nūr al-Dīn and Anīs al-Jalīs, called here by their youth.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ نُورُ الدِّينِ وَاللَّهِ يَاصَيَّادُ أَتَيْتَنَا بِفَضِيلَةٍ مَلِيحَةٍ فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Nūru al-Dīni wa-Allāhi yā-ṣayyādu ataytanā bi-faḍīlatin malīḥatin fī hādhihi al-laylati
sentences.l: And Nūr al-Dīn said: By-God, O fisherman, you-came-to-us with a fine excellence in this night.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn said, "By God, fisherman, you have brought us a handsome favour this night."
sentences.n: أتى بـ is "bring": the verb chooses the preposition, so أتيتنا بفضيلة is "you came to us with a favour", that is, "you did us a kindness".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ وَضَعَ يَدَهُ فِي جَيْبِهِ وَأَخْرَجَ لَهُ ثَلٰثَةَ دَنَانِيرَ مِنَ الدَّنَانِيرِ الَّتِي أَعْطَاهُمْ لَهُ سَنْجَرُ وَقْتَ خُرُوجِهِ لِلسَّفَرِ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا صَيَّادُ اِعْذُرْنِي فَوَاللَّهِ لَوْ عَرَفْتَنِي قَبْلَ الَّذِي حَصَلَ لِي لَكُنْتُ نَزَعْتُ مَرَارَةَ الْفَقْرِ مِنْ قَلْبِكَ لَكِنْ خُذْ هَذَا عَلَى حَسَبِ الْبَرَكَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma waḍaʿa yadahu fī jaybihi wa-akhraja lahu thalāthata danānīra mina al-danānīri allatī aʿṭāhum lahu Sanjaru waqta khurūjihi li-al-safari wa-qāla lahu yā ṣayyādu iʿdhurnī fa-wa-Allāhi law ʿaraftanī qabla alladhī ḥaṣala lī la-kuntu nazaʿtu marārata al-faqri min qalbika lākin khudh hādhā ʿalā ḥasabi al-baraka
sentences.l: Then he put his hand in his pocket and brought-out for-him three dinars, of the dinars which gave-them to-him Sanjar at-the-time of-his-going-out for-the-journey; and he said to him: O fisherman, excuse me; for by-God, if you had-known me before that which happened to me, I would-have removed the bitterness of-poverty from your heart. But take this according-to the blessing.
sentences.i: Then he put his hand into his pocket and drew out for him three dinars, from the dinars that Sanjar had given him when he set out on his journey. "Fisherman," he said, "forgive me. By God, had you known me before what befell me, I would have plucked the bitterness of poverty from your heart. But take this, as God's blessing allows."
sentences.n: The print has ثلثة without the alif of ثلاثة; the dagger alif marks the missing long ā. اعطاهم له is the print's "gave them to him", with a plural pronoun for the dinars, as often in the Nights. The sense of لو عرفتني is that, had the fisherman only met him in his days of wealth, he would have given far more; I translate what is printed. على حسب البركة is "according to the measure of the blessing", that is, "as much as God has left me".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ رَمَاهُمْ لِلْخَلِيفَةِ فَأَخَذَهُمُ الْخَلِيفَةُ وَبَاسَهُمْ وَشَالَهُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma ramāhum li-al-khalīfati fa-akhadhahumu al-khalīfatu wa-bāsahum wa-shālahum
sentences.l: Then he threw-them to-the-caliph, and took-them the caliph, and kissed-them, and lifted-them.
sentences.i: Then he tossed them to the caliph, who took them, kissed them, and tucked them away.
sentences.n: باس ("kissed") and شال ("lifted, carried off") are colloquial verbs, kissing a gift being a mark of respect for the giver.

sentences.t: وَمَا كَانَ مُرَادُ الْخَلِيفَةِ بِذَلِكَ إِلَّا السَّمَاعَ مِنَ الْجَارِيَةِ وَهِيَ تُغَنِّي
sentences.tr: wa-mā kāna murādu al-khalīfati bi-dhālika illā al-samāʿa mina al-jāriyati wa-hiya tughannī
sentences.l: And not was the aim of-the-caliph by that except the hearing from the slave-girl, and she sings.
sentences.i: But the caliph's whole aim in this was only to hear the girl as she sang.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْخَلِيفَةُ أَحْسَنْتَ وَتَفَضَّلْتَ لَكِنْ مُرَادِي مِنْ تَفَضُّلَاتِكَ الْعَمِيمَةِ أَنَّ هَذِهِ الْجَارِيَةَ تُغَنِّي لَنَا صَوْتًا حَتَّى أَسْمَعَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-khalīfatu aḥsanta wa-tafaḍḍalta lākin murādī min tafaḍḍulātika al-ʿamīmati anna hādhihi al-jāriyata tughannī lanā ṣawtan ḥattā asmaʿahā
sentences.l: And the caliph said to him: You did-well and showed-favour; but my aim from your abundant favours (is) that this slave-girl sing for-us a song, until I hear her.
sentences.i: The caliph said to him, "You have done well and shown generosity; but what I ask of your overflowing kindness is that this girl sing us a song, that I may hear her."
sentences.n: صوتا is "a song" (a vocal piece); the verb تغني is a bare present where Classical would use أن with the subjunctive, "that she sing".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ نُورُ الدِّينِ عَلِيٌّ يَا أَنِيسَ الْجَلِيسِ قَالَتْ نَعَمْ قَالَ لَهَا بِحَيَاتِي غَنِّي لَنَا شَيْأً مِنْ شَانِ خَاطِرِ هَذَا الصَّيَّادِ لِأَنَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَسْمَعَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Nūru al-Dīni ʿAliyyun yā-Anīsa al-Jalīsi qālat naʿam qāla lahā bi-ḥayātī ghannī lanā shayʾan min shāni khāṭiri hādhā al-ṣayyādi li-annahu yurīdu an yasmaʿaki
sentences.l: And Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī said: O Anīs al-Jalīs. She said: Yes. He said to-her: By my-life, sing for-us something for the sake of the mind of-this fisherman, because he wants that he-hear you.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī said, "Anīs al-Jalīs." "Yes," she said. "By my life," said he, "sing us something to please this fisherman, for he wishes to hear you."
sentences.n: بحياتي is an oath, "by my life". من شان خاطر is "for the sake of the feelings of", that is, to please him. The أ of شيأ is the print's own and kept precomposed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ كَلَامَ سَيِّدِهَا أَخَذَتِ الْعُودَ وَحَرَّكَتْهُ بَعْدَ أَنْ أَصْلَحَتْ أَوْ تَارَهُ وَأَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿati al-jāriyatu kalāma sayyidihā akhadhati al-ʿūda wa-ḥarrakat-hu baʿda an aṣlaḥat aw tārahu wa-anshadat taqūlu
sentences.l: And when heard the slave-girl the speech of-her-master, she took the lute and moved-it after she set-right its strings, and recited, saying:
sentences.i: When the girl heard her master's words she took up the lute, and, having tuned its strings, she set it sounding and recited, saying:
sentences.n: The line-break splits أوتاره ("its strings") into او and تاره; I keep the print's two tokens and point them as pieces of that one word. حركته, "she moved it", means that she played it.

sentences.t:
وَغَادَةٍ مَسَكَتْ لِلْعُودِ أَنْمُلُهَا * فَعَادَتِ النَّفْسُ عِنْدَ الْجَسِّ تَخْتَلِسُ
غَنَّتْ فَابْرَى غِنَاهَا مَنْ بِهِ صَمَمُ * وَقَالَ أَحْسَنْتَ حَقًّا مَنْ بِهِ خَرَسُ
sentences.tr:
wa-ghādatin masakat li-al-ʿūdi anmuluhā * fa-ʿādati al-nafsu ʿinda al-jassi takhtalisu
ghannat fa-abrā ghināhā man bihi ṣamamu * wa-qāla aḥsanta ḥaqqan man bihi kharasu
sentences.l:
And (many) a lovely-girl whose fingertips gripped the lute, * so the soul, at the touch, became snatched-away;
she sang, and her song healed him in-whom (was) deafness, * and said "You did well, truly" he in-whom (was) dumbness.
sentences.i: Many a lovely girl whose fingertips closed upon the lute, * so that at their touch the soul is carried off; she sang, and her song cured the deaf man, * and the dumb man cried, "Well done, truly!"
sentences.n: Verse, copied as pointed in the print; every word is marked there, so nothing is added. The opening وَ is the wāw that means "many a" (rubba). فَابْرَى is printed with a bare alif: it is for فَأَبْرَأَ, "healed", and I leave it as printed. تَخْتَلِسُ is the print's pointing, "is snatched away", a verb in the passive sense. حَقًّا and the pointing of the second hemistich are as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا ضَرَبَتْ ضَرْبًا بَدِيعًا إِلَى أَنْ أَذْهَلَتِ الْعُقُولَ وَأَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتِ الْأَبْيَاتِ شِعْـــرَ —
sentences.tr: thumma innahā ḍarabat ḍarban badīʿan ilā an adhhalati al-ʿuqūla wa-anshadat taqūlu hādhihi al-abyāti al-abyāti shiʿra —
sentences.l: Then indeed-she struck a striking, wondrous, until she bewildered the minds; and she recited, saying, these the-verses the-verses, (in) poetry:
sentences.i: Then she played a marvellous strain upon the lute, until she had bewildered every mind; and she sang, reciting these verses:
sentences.n: ضربت ضربا is “she struck a striking”, and the sense is that she played an instrument (the lute, understood); no instrument is named here. The print repeats الابيات twice in a row across a line break; both are kept as printed, and the second adds nothing. The dash after شعر is the print's own mark, kept at the end of the unit. The print ends شعر with a stretched letter and no alif, so I vocalise it as a bare accusative, “(in) verse”, as in the previous night; the verse follows.

sentences.t:
وَلَقَــدْ شُرِفْنَا اِذْ نَزَلْتُمْ اَرْضَنَا * وَمَحَا سَنَاكُمْ ظُلْمَةَ الدَّيْجُورِ
فَحَقٌّ لِي اِنِّي اُخَلِّقُ مَنْزِلِي * بِالْمِسْكِ وَالْمَا وَرْدِ الْكَافُورِ
sentences.tr:
wa-laqad shurifnā idh nazaltum arḍanā * wa-maḥā sanākum ẓulmata al-daymūri
fa-ḥaqqun lī innī ukhalliqu manzilī * bi-al-miski wa-al-mā wardi al-kāfūri
sentences.l:
And indeed we-were-honoured when you-alighted (in) our-land, * and effaced your-radiance the-darkness of-the-gloom;
so right (is) to-me that-I perfume my-dwelling * with-the-musk and-the-water, rose, the-camphor.
sentences.i: We are honoured indeed by your coming down into our land, * and your radiance has blotted out the darkness of the night. It is only right that I perfume my dwelling * with musk and rose-water and camphor.
sentences.n: Verse, copied as pointed in the print; every word is marked there, so nothing is added. The print stretches وَلَقَــدْ with a tatweel; it is kept. أُخَلِّقُ is “I anoint with khalūq (a saffron perfume)”, here simply “perfume”. الما is printed without its hamza (for الماء, “water”), and the line then runs المَا وَرْدِ الكَافُورِ with no conjunction before “camphor”; I read “rose-water” as one thing and “camphor” as a second, in apposition, and translate with “and”.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ اضْطَرَبَ الْخَلِيفَةُ وَغَلَبَ عَلَيْهِ الْوَجْدُ فَلَمْ يَتَمَالَكْ نَفْسَهُ مِنْ شِدَّةِ الطَّرَبِ إِلَى أَنْ قَالَ وَاللَّهِ طَيِّبٌ وَاللَّهِ طَيِّبٌ وَاللَّهِ طَيِّبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika iḍṭaraba al-khalīfatu wa-ghalaba ʿalayhi al-wajdu fa-lam yatamālak nafsahu min shiddati al-ṭarabi ilā an qāla wa-Allāhi ṭayyibun wa-Allāhi ṭayyibun wa-Allāhi ṭayyibun
sentences.l: And at that, was-agitated the caliph, and overcame upon-him the ecstasy, and he did not contain himself from the intensity of-the-rapture, until he said: By-God (it is) good, by-God (it is) good, by-God (it is) good.
sentences.i: At that the caliph was shaken, and ecstasy overcame him, so that he could not contain himself for the sheer intensity of his delight, until he cried out, “By God, it is fine! By God, it is fine! By God, it is fine!”
sentences.n: The caliph is still in the disguise of the fisherman Karīm, and has been listening to the girl sing. طيب here is “fine, excellent”. يتمالك is jussive after لم, so it ends in a sukūn.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ نُورُ الدِّينِ يَا صَيَّادُ هَلْ أَعْجَبَتْكَ الْجَارِيَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Nūru al-Dīni yā ṣayyādu hal aʿjabatka al-jāriyatu
sentences.l: And said Nūr al-Dīn: O fisherman, did-it-please-you the slave-girl?
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn said, “Fisherman, does the girl please you?”
sentences.n: Nūr al-Dīn addresses the caliph as “fisherman” because he believes he is one; the caliph has come to the garden in the guise of the fisherman Karīm. The print joins نور الدين into one word, نورالدين; it is kept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ إِي وَاللَّهِ فَقَالَ نُورُ الدِّينِ هِيَ هِبَةٌ مِنِّي إِلَيْكَ هِبَةَ كَرِيمٍ لَايُرَدُّ فِي عَطَائِهِ وَلَا يَرْجِعُ فِي هِبَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu ī wa-Allāhi fa-qāla Nūru al-Dīni hiya hibatun minnī ilayka hibata karīmin lā yuraddu fī ʿaṭāʾihi wa-lā yarjiʿu fī hibatihi
sentences.l: And said the caliph: Yes, by-God. And said Nūr al-Dīn: She (is) a gift from-me to-you, the-gift of-a-generous-one who is-not-turned-back in his-giving, and does-not take-back his-gift.
sentences.i: The caliph said, “Yes, by God.” And Nūr al-Dīn said, “She is a gift from me to you, the gift of a generous man who is never denied in his giving and never takes back his gift.”
sentences.n: The print joins لايرد into one word. يرد is vocalised as a passive, “is turned back, refused”, which suits “in his giving”; the other possibility would be to read it as active, “does not turn (anyone) back”, which also makes sense. The print spells عطائه with a precomposed hamza on a yāʾ-seat, which is kept. إي والله is a common asseveration, “yes, by God”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ نُورَ الدِّينِ نَهَضَ قَائِمًا عَلَى قَدَمَيْهِ وَأَخَذَ مُلُوطَةً وَرَمَاهَا عَلَى الصَّيَّادِ وَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ وَيَرُوحَ بِالْجَارِيَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna Nūra al-Dīni nahaḍa qāʾiman ʿalā qadamayhi wa-akhadha mulūṭatan wa-ramāhā ʿalā al-ṣayyādi wa-amarahu an yakhruja wa-yarūḥa bi-al-jāriyati
sentences.l: Then indeed Nūr al-Dīn rose, standing upon his-two-feet, and took a mulūṭa and threw-it upon the fisherman, and commanded-him that he-go-out and depart with-the-slave-girl.
sentences.i: Then Nūr al-Dīn rose to his feet, took up a cloak and threw it over the fisherman, and bade him go out and be off with the girl.
sentences.n: ملوطة is a kind of outer garment, a cloak or mantle; the word is rare, and I translate it by its use here, as a robe thrown over the man as a gift of honour. In the print, قائما has a precomposed hamza, which is kept. يروح بـ is “to go off with, take away”.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ إِلَيْهِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا سَيِّدِي أَنْتَ رَائِحٌ بِلَا وَدَاعٍ إِنْ كَانَ وَلَابُدَّ فَقِفْ حَتَّى أُوَدِّعَكَ وَأَشْرَحُ حَالِي
sentences.tr: fa-naẓarati al-jāriyatu ilayhi wa-qālat lahu yā sayyidī anta rāʾiḥun bi-lā wadāʿin in kāna wa-lā budda fa-qif ḥattā uwadditaka wa-ashraḥu ḥālī
sentences.l: And looked the slave-girl at-him, and said to-him: O my-master, you (are) departing without farewell. If it-is, and (there is) no escape, then stand until I-bid-you-farewell and I-explain my-state.
sentences.i: The girl looked at him and said, “My lord, are you going without a farewell? If it must be, and there is no way out, then wait until I take my leave of you and tell you how I stand.”
sentences.n: The slave-girl, Anīs al-Jalīs, speaks to her master Nūr al-Dīn, whom she calls “my lord”, not to the fisherman. إن كان ولابد is a set phrase meaning “if it must be so”. The print gives اشرحُ a damma on the ḥāʾ, kept here; it makes the verb indicative, “and I explain”, where Classical would expect the subjunctive after حتى.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنْشَدَتْ وَجَعَلَتْ تَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتِ شِعْـــرَ
sentences.tr: thumma anshadat wa-jaʿalat taqūlu hādhihi al-abyāti shiʿra
sentences.l: Then she recited, and began saying these the-verses, (in) poetry:
sentences.i: Then she sang, and went on to recite these verses:
sentences.n: Again the print stretches شعر with a tatweel and no alif; see the note on the first verse of this night.

sentences.t:
عِنْدِي مِنَ الشَّوْقِ وَالتَّذْكَارِ وَالْبَرَحَا * مَاصَيَّرَ الْجِسْمَ مِنْ فَرْطِ الضَّنَى شَبَحًا
اَحْبَابَنَا لَا تَقُولُوا لِي سَلُوتَكُمْ * وَالْحَالُ بِالْحَالِ وَالتَّبْرِيحُ مَابَرِحَا
لَوْ كَانَ يَسْبَحُ حَيٌّ فِي مَدَامِعِهِ * لَكُنْتُ اَوَّلَ مَنْ فِي دَمْعِهِ سَبَحَا
يَا مَنْ تَحَكَّمَ فِي قَلْبِي مَحَبَّتُكُمْ * كَمَا تَحَكَّمَ مَزْجُ الْخَمْرِ بِالْقَدَحَا
هَذَا الْفِرَاقُ الَّذِي قَدْ كُنْتُ اَحْذَرُهُ * يَا مَنْ هَوَاهُ بِقَلْبِي وَالْحَشَا مَزَحَا
يَا بْنَ خَاقَانَ يَا سُولِي وَيَا اَمَلِي * يَا مَنْ هَوَاهُ بِقَلْبِي قَطُّ مَا بَرِحَا
قَدْ كُنْتَ عَادَيْتَ مَوْلَانَا وَسَيِّدَنَا * لِاَجْلِي وَعُدْتَ عَنِ الْاَوْطَانِ مُنْتَزِحَا
لَا اَوْحَشَ اللّٰهُ مِنْ سِيدِي عَلَى فَقْدِي * وَهَبْتَنِي لِكَرِيمٍ ظَلَّ مُمْتَدِحَا
sentences.tr:
ʿindī mina al-shawqi wa-al-tadhkāri wa-al-baraḥā * mā ṣayyara al-jisma min farṭi al-ḍanā shabaḥā
aḥbābanā lā taqūlū lī salūwatakum * wa-al-ḥālu bi-al-ḥāli wa-al-tabrīḥu mā baraḥā
law kāna yasbaḥu ḥayyun fī madāmiʿihi * la-kuntu awwala man fī damʿihi sabaḥā
yā man taḥakkama fī qalbī maḥabbatukum * kamā taḥakkama mazju al-khamri bi-al-qadaḥā
hādhā al-firāqu alladhī qad kuntu aḥdharuhu * yā man hawāhu bi-qalbī wa-al-ḥashā mazaḥā
yā ibna Khāqāna yā sūlī wa-yā amalī * yā man hawāhu bi-qalbī qaṭṭu mā baraḥā
qad kunta ʿādayta mawlānā wa-sayyidanā * li-ajlī wa-ʿudta ʿani al-awṭāni muntaziḥā
lā awḥasha Allāhu min sīdī ʿalā faqdī * wahabtanī li-karīmin ẓalla mumtadiḥā
sentences.l:
I-have of the-longing and-the-remembrance and-the-anguish * what made the-body, from excess of-wasting, a-phantom.
O our-beloved-ones, do not say to-me your-forgetting; * the-state (is) as-the-state, and the-anguish has-not ceased.
If a-living-one could-swim in his-tears, * I-would-be the-first of-those who in his-tear swam.
O you, in my-heart holds-sway your-love, * as holds-sway the-mixing of-the-wine over-the-cup;
this (is) the-parting that I-was dreading it, * O you whose-love (is) in-my-heart and-the-vitals — has-sported.
O son-of Khāqān, O my-desire and-O my-hope, * O you whose-love in-my-heart has never at-all left;
you had been-hostile to-our-lord and-our-master * for-my-sake, and you-turned from the-homelands, far-removed.
May-not God make-desolate my-master over my-loss: * you-gave-me to-a-generous-one who-remained praising.
sentences.i: Within me are such longing, remembrance and anguish * as have turned the body, from the excess of wasting, to a mere phantom. O my beloved ones, do not speak to me of forgetting you; * my state is as it was, and the anguish has not left me. If any living creature could swim in its own tears, * I would be the first to have swum in mine. O you whose love holds sway in my heart, * as the mingling of wine holds sway in the cup: this is the parting that I always dreaded, * O you whose passion plays through my heart and vitals. O son of Khāqān, my wish and my hope, * O you whose love has never at all left my heart, you made an enemy of our lord and master * for my sake, and you went far from your homeland, a man removed. May God not leave my master desolate for losing me: * you gave me to a generous man who remains full of praise.
sentences.n: Verse, copied as pointed in the print; every word is marked there, so nothing is added. Several rhyme words end in the alif of the poetic accusative, which carries no case here but only holds the rhyme in -aḥā: البرحا، شبحا، سبحا، القدحا، مزحا، برحا، منتزحا، ممتدحا. In line 6 the print has يا بْنَ with a sukūn on the bāʾ, to be read “yā-bna”. In line 4, the verb تَحَكَّمَ takes في for the place and بـ for the thing controlled; “holds sway over the cup” is how I take the second. مَزَحَا in line 5 is obscure to me: the sense is probably “played, sported”, as a love that moves about the heart; the line also repeats the second half of line 6. In line 7, عُدْتَ عَنِ is hard to place; I take it as “you turned away from, left”. In the last line, لَا أَوْحَشَ اللّٰهُ is a prayer, “may God not make desolate”, and ممتدحا is printed with kasra on the dāl, active, “praising”; the sense of the closing line is uncertain, and I give it as it stands. سيدي is printed سِيدِي (no yāʾ-doubling), for sayyidī.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَتْ مِنْ شِعْرِهَا أَجَابَهَا نُورُالدِّينِ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ شِعْـــــرًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghat min shiʿrihā ajābahā Nūru al-Dīni wa-huwa yaqūlu shiʿran
sentences.l: And when she finished from her-poetry, answered-her Nūr al-Dīn, and he (was) saying (in) verse:
sentences.i: When she had finished her verses, Nūr al-Dīn answered her in verse, saying:
sentences.n: The print joins نورالدين into one word; it is kept. شعرا is an accusative of the thing said, “in verse”, with its tanwīn alif here.

sentences.t:
وَدَّعَتْنِي يَوْمَ الْفِرَاقِ وَقَالَتْ * وَهْيَ تَبْكِي مِنْ لَوْعَةِ الْاِشْتِيَاقِ
مَا الَّذِي اَنْتَ صَانِعٌ بَعْدَ بَعْدِي * قُلْتُ قُولِي هَذَا لِمَنْ هُوَ بَاقِ
sentences.tr:
waddaʿatnī yawma al-firāqi wa-qālat * wa-hya tabkī min lawʿati al-ishtiyāqi
mā alladhī anta ṣāniʿun baʿda baʿdī * qultu qūlī hādhā li-man huwa bāqī
sentences.l:
She-bade-me-farewell on-the-day of-the-parting and-said, * and-she weeping from the-burning of-the-yearning:
What (is) that which you (are) doing after my-being-far? * I-said: Say this to-one who he (is) remaining.
sentences.i: She bade me farewell on the day of parting, and said, * weeping for the burn of longing: What will you do after I am gone? * I said: Say that to one who will remain.
sentences.n: Verse, copied as pointed in the print; every word is marked there, so nothing is added. وَهْيَ is the print's pointing of the contracted wa-hya. بَعْدَ بَعْدِي is a play on words: “after my being far (from you)”. The last line is a riddle: “say this to the one who remains”, in other words, “ask someone who will outlive the parting; I shall not”. The final hemistich ends with the elided form باقِ for bāqin.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ لَمَّا سَمِعَ الْخَلِيفَةُ قَوْلَهَا فِي شِعْرِهَا وَهَبْتَنِي الْكَرِيمَ ازْدَادَ فِيهَا رَغْبَتُهُ وَصَعُبَ عَلَيْهِ التَّفْرِيقُ بَيْنَهُمَا وَعَزَّ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu lammā samiʿa al-khalīfatu qawlahā fī shiʿrihā wahabtanī al-karīma izdāda fīhā raghbatuhu wa-ṣaʿuba ʿalayhi al-tafrīqu baynahumā wa-ʿazza ʿalayhi
sentences.l: Then indeed-he, when heard the caliph her-saying in her-poetry “you-gave-me the-generous-one”, increased in her his-desire, and was-hard upon-him the-separating between-the-two-of-them, and was-grievous upon-him.
sentences.i: Now when the caliph heard her say in her verses, “You gave me to the generous”, his desire for her grew greater; it grieved him to part the two of them, and it weighed hard upon him.
sentences.n: ثم انه لما سمع is the Middle Arabic habit of starting a clause with “then indeed-he” and carrying the subject after the verb; I translate it as ordinary narrative. The caliph quotes the end of her verse, وهبتني لكريم, but the print drops the lām and leaves الكريم as a direct object; I vocalise what is printed. In the print, ازداد فيها رغبته has the verb with a feminine-looking subject, with رغبته the subject (“his desire increased”); the construction is loose and I keep it. The shadda on عزّ is printed.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ الْمُصْبِي يَاسَيِّدِي إِنَّ هَذِهِ الْجَارِيَةَ قَٰلْ ذَكَرَتْ فِي شِعْرِهَا أَنَّكَ عَادَيْتَ لِسَيِّدِهَا وَمَنْ مَلَكَهَا فَأَخْبِرْنِي أَنْتَ لِمَنْ عَادَيْتَ وَلِمَنْ لَهُ عَلَيْكَ طَلَبٌ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla al-muṣbī yā sayyidī inna hādhihi al-jāriyata qāl dhakarat fī shiʿrihā annaka ʿādayta li-sayyidihā wa-man malakahā fa-akhbirnī anta li-man ʿādayta wa-li-man lahu ʿalayka ṭalabun
sentences.l: And said the fisherman (printed al-muṣbī, a misprint for al-ṣayyād): O my-master, indeed this the-slave-girl, [qāl] she-mentioned in her-poetry that-you were-hostile to-her-master and-whoever owned-her; so inform-me, you, to-whom you-were-hostile, and to-whom has against-you a-claim.
sentences.i: The fisherman said, “My lord, this girl has said in her verses that you made an enemy of her master and of the one who owned her. So tell me, whom did you make your enemy, and who has a claim against you?”
sentences.n: المصبي is a puzzle: it must mean the fisherman, الصياد, and is probably a misprint. I vocalise the letters as printed, al-muṣbī, and translate by the sense. The print has قل before ذكرت; the true reading is probably قد, “has”, with a printer's slip, and I point it قَٰلْ, with the dagger alif that marks a defective spelling, and read the sense as “she has mentioned”. عاديت لسيدها has an odd lām after “be hostile to”, taking the dative where Classical has the direct object; it is Middle Arabic, kept as it stands.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ نُورُالدِّينِ وَاللَّهِ يَاصَيَّادُ جَرَى لِي وَلِهَذِهِ الْجَارِيَةِ حَدِيثٌ عَجِيبٌ وَأَمْرٌ غَرِيبٌ لَوْ كُتِبَ بِالْإِبَرِ عَلَى آمَاقِ الْبَصَرِ لَكَانَ عِبْرَةً لِمَنِ اعْتَبَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Nūru al-Dīni wa-Allāhi yā ṣayyādu jarā lī wa-li-hādhihi al-jāriyati ḥadīthun ʿajībun wa-amrun gharībun law kutiba bi-al-ibari ʿalā āmāqi al-baṣari la-kāna ʿibratan li-mani iʿtabara
sentences.l: And said Nūr al-Dīn: By-God, O fisherman, there-happened to-me and-to-this the-slave-girl a-tale wondrous and-a-matter strange; if it-were-written with-the-needles upon the-corners of-the-eye, it-would-be a-lesson for-whoever takes-heed.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn said, “By God, fisherman, a wondrous tale and a strange affair has befallen me and this girl. Were it written with needles on the corners of the eyes, it would be a lesson to whoever takes heed.”
sentences.n: A set boast for a tale of marvels: it is so remarkable that, if it were pricked with needles into the inner corners of the eye, it would still be a warning to those who can take one. The print joins ياصياد into one word. آماق (sing. مؤق) is printed with a precomposed آ, which is kept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ أَمَا تُحَدِّثُنَا بِمَا جَرَى لَكَ مِنْ حَدِيثِكَ وَتُعَرِّفُنَا بِخَبَرِكَ عَسَى أَنْ يَكُونَ لَكَ فِيهِ فَرَجٌ فَإِنَّ فَرَجَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu amā tuḥaddithunā bi-mā jarā laka min ḥadīthika wa-tuʿarrifunā bi-khabarika ʿasā an yakūna laka fīhi farajun fa-inna faraja Allāhi qarībun
sentences.l: And said the caliph: Will-you-not tell-us of what happened to-you, of your-tale, and make-us-know your-news? Perhaps there-will-be for-you in it relief; for indeed the-relief of-God (is) near.
sentences.i: The caliph said, “Will you not tell us what has happened to you, and let us know your story? Perhaps there will be relief for you in it, for the relief of God is near.”
sentences.n: بما جرى is “of what happened”: the verb حدّث takes بـ for the thing told. من حديثك is “(that is) from your tale”, a loose apposition. The last clause is a proverbial comfort: God's relief is never far.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ نُورُالدِّينِ يَا صَيَّادُ هَلْ تَسْمَعُ حَدِيثَنَا نَظْمًا أَوْ نَثْرًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Nūru al-Dīni yā ṣayyādu hal tasmaʿu ḥadīthanā naẓman aw nathran
sentences.l: And said Nūr al-Dīn: O fisherman, will-you-hear our-tale (as) verse or prose?
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn said, “Fisherman, will you hear our story in verse or in prose?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ النَّثْرُ كَلَامٌ وَالشِّعْرُ نِظَامٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu al-nathru kalāmun wa-al-shiʿru niẓāmun
sentences.l: And said the caliph: The-prose (is) speech, and-the-poetry (is) order.
sentences.i: The caliph said, “Prose is speech, and verse is a string of pearls.”
sentences.n: نظام is the string on which pearls are threaded, hence “order, arrangement”; the caliph is saying that verse is to prose as strung pearls are to loose ones. I give the image in the idiomatic layer; the literal layer keeps “order”.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَطْرَقَ نُورُالدِّينِ رَأْسَهُ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتِ شِــعْـــرَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika aṭraqa Nūru al-Dīni raʾsahu ilā al-arḍi wa-anshada yaqūlu hādhihi al-abyāti shiʿra
sentences.l: And at that Nūr al-Dīn bowed his-head to the-earth, and recited, saying, these the-verses, (in) poetry:
sentences.i: Thereupon Nūr al-Dīn bowed his head to the ground and recited these verses:
sentences.n: The print has رأسه with a precomposed hamza on the alif, which is kept; the print stretches شعر with tatweels and no alif, and the verse that follows begins the next slice.

sentences.t:
يَاخَلِيلِي اِنِّي هَجَرْتُ رُقَادِي * وَتَزَايَدَ هَمِّي لِبُعْدِ بِلَادِي
وَالِدُ كَانَ لِي عَلَيَّ شَفُوقَا * غَابَ عَنِّي وَجَاوَرَ الْاَلْحَادِ
فَاتَتْ بَعْدَهُ عَلَيَّ اُمُورٌ * صِرْتُ مِنْهَا مُفَتِّتَ الْاَكْبَادِ
اِشْتَرَى لِي مِنَ الْجَوَارِي خُودًا * يُخْجِلُ الْغُصْنَ قَدُّهَا الْمَيَّادِ
فَصَرَفْتُ الَّذِي وَرِثْتُ عَلَيْهَا * وَتَكَرَّمْتُ بِهِ عَلَى الْاَجْوَادِ
سِمْتُهَا الْبَيْعَ اِذْ تَزَايَدَ هَمِّي * وَجَوَى الْبَيْنِ لَمْ يَكُنْ بِمُرَادِي
وَاِذَا مَادَ عَا اِلَيْهَا مُنَادٍ * زَادَ فِيهَا شَيْخٌ كَثِيرُ الْفَسَادِ
فَلِهَذَا اِغْتَظْتُ غَيْظًا شَدِيدًا * وَنَتَرْتُ يَدَهَا مِنْ يَدِ الْاَوْغَادِ
فَلَكَمَنِي هَذَا اللَّئِيمُ بِغَيْظٍ * ثُمَّ قَادَتْ فِيهِ لَظَى الْاِلْحَادِ
فَلَكَمْتُهُ مِنْ حُرْقَتِي بِيَمِينِي * وَشِمَالِي حَتَّى شَفَيْتُ فُؤَادِي
وَمِنَ الْخَوْفِ قَدْ اَتَيْتُ لِدَارِي * وَتَغَيَّبْتُ خِيفَةَ الْاَضْدَادِ
فَاَمَرَ حَاكِمُ الْبِلَادِ بِمَسْكِي * فَاَتَى الْحَاجِبُ الْكَثِيرُ السَّدَادِ
رَامِزَالِي اِنِّي اَسِيرُ بَعِيدًا * وَاَغِيبُ عَنْهُمْ وَاكْمُدُ الْحُسَّادِي
فَطَلَعْنَا مِنْ دَارِنَا جِنْحَ لَيْلٍ * طَالِبِينَا الْمَقَامَ فِي بَغْدَادِ
لَيْسَ شَيْءٌ مِنَ الذَّخَائِرِ عِنْدِي * اُعْطِيكَ غَيْرَ مَا وَهَبْتُ يَا صَيَّادِ
غَيْرَ اِنِّي اُعْطِيكَ مُحْبُوبَ قَلْبِي * فَتَيَقَّنْ اِنِّي وَهَبْتُ فُؤادِي
sentences.tr:
yā khalīlī innī hajartu ruqādī * wa-tazāyada hammī li-buʿdi bilādī
wālidu kāna lī ʿalayya shafūqā * ghāba ʿannī wa-jāwara al-alḥādi
fātat baʿdahu ʿalayya umūrun * ṣirtu minhā mufattita al-akbādi
ishtarā lī mina al-jawārī khūdan * yukhjilu al-ghuṣna qadduhā al-mayyādi
fa-ṣaraftu alladhī warithtu ʿalayhā * wa-takarramtu bihi ʿalā al-ajwādi
simtuhā al-bayʿa idh tazāyada hammī * wa-jawā al-bayni lam yakun bi-murādī
wa-idhā māda ʿā ilayhā munādin * zāda fīhā shaykhun kathīru al-fasādi
fa-li-hādhā ightaztu ghayẓan shadīdan * wa-nataratu yadahā min yadi al-awghādi
fa-lakamanī hādhā al-laʾīmu bi-ghayẓin * thumma qādat fīhi laẓā al-ilḥādi
fa-lakamtuhu min ḥurqatī bi-yamīnī * wa-shimālī ḥattā shafaytu fuʾādī
wa-mina al-khawfi qad atītu li-dārī * wa-taghayyabtu khīfata al-aḍdādi
fa-amara ḥākimu al-bilādi bi-maskī * fa-atā al-ḥājibu al-kathīru al-sadādi
rāmizan lī innī asīru baʿīdan * wa-aghību ʿanhum wa-akmudu al-ḥussādī
fa-ṭalaʿnā min dārinā jinḥa laylin * ṭālibīnā al-maqāma fī Baghdādi
laysa shayʾun mina al-dhakhāʾiri ʿindī * uʿṭīka ghayra mā wahabtu yā ṣayyādi
ghayra innī uʿṭīka maḥbūba qalbī * fa-tayaqqan innī wahabtu fuʾādī
sentences.i:
O my friend, I have forsaken sleep, and my anguish has grown for the distance of my homeland.
I had a father who was tender toward me; he departed from me and dwells beside the graves.
After him there came upon me such affairs that they left me with a heart broken to pieces.
He had bought me, from among the slave-girls, a fair maiden whose swaying figure shames the bough.
I spent my inheritance upon her, and lavished it upon the open-handed.
I put her up for sale when my anguish grew, though the ache of parting was not my wish;
and when a crier called her, a shaykh, abounding in vileness, bid higher for her.
Therefore I was seized by a fierce rage, and snatched her hand out of the hand of that low wretch.
That base fellow struck me in his fury, and the flame of wickedness blazed up in him;
so out of my burning I struck him with my right hand and my left, until I had eased my heart.
Then in fear I came to my house and hid myself for dread of my foes;
the ruler of the land ordered me seized, and the chamberlain, a man of great uprightness, came,
hinting to me that I should go far away and vanish from them, and so grieve the envious.
So we left our house in the dark of night, seeking a dwelling in Baghdad.
I have no store of treasures to give you beyond what I have given, fisherman,
except that I give you the beloved of my heart; be sure that I have given my very heart.
sentences.n: Verse, copied as pointed in the print; every word is marked there, so nothing is added. The poem is Nūr al-Dīn's answer to the disguised caliph, here called ṣayyād, “fisherman”. The print has several oddities, kept as printed. يَاخَلِيلِي and رَامِزَالِي are each run together. مَادَ عَا is the single word دعا (with ما: “whenever … called”) cut in two by a space. فَاتَتْ has no hamza and reads best as فَأَتَتْ, “then there came upon”. قَادَتْ is probably قَدَتْ, “blazed”, with the alif spelled out. الْمَيَّادِ has a kasra for the rhyme where the agreement with قدّها would be nominative. وَاكْمُدُ is printed with damma; the sense is “cause grief to”, and the stray final yā of الْحُسَّادِي fits the rhyme and may be the pronoun “my”. In line 2 الْاَلْحَادِ is alḥād, “graves”, and in line 9 الْاِلْحَادِ is ilḥād, “impiety”, two different words. At the end, the beloved he offers the fisherman is Anīs al-Jalīs, the girl.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ قَالَ لَهُ الْخَلِيفَةُ يَا سَيِّدِي نُورَالدِّينِ اِشْرَحْ لِي أَمْرَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min shiʿrihi qāla lahu al-khalīfatu yā sayyidī Nūra al-Dīni ishraḥ lī amraka
sentences.l: And when he finished from his-poetry, said to-him the caliph: O my-lord Nūr al-Dīn, expound to-me your-affair.
sentences.i: When he had finished his verses, the caliph said to him, “My lord Nūr al-Dīn, set out your story for me.”
sentences.n: The print joins نورالدين into one word, as throughout. The caliph is still in the fisherman's disguise (as Karīm), and he calls Nūr al-Dīn sayyidī, “my lord”, which is simply courteous address. فرغ من is “finish with”.

sentences.t: فَأَخْبَرَهُ نُورُالدِّينِ بِخَبَرِهِ مِنْ مُبْتَدَأِ الْأَمْرِ إِلَى مُنْتَهَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-akhbarahu Nūru al-Dīni bi-khabarihi min mubtadaʾi al-amri ilā muntahāhu
sentences.l: And informed-him Nūr al-Dīn with his-account from the beginning of-the-affair to its-end.
sentences.i: So Nūr al-Dīn told him his tale, from the beginning of the affair to its end.
sentences.n: أخبر بـ takes the thing told with bi-: “informed him of his news”. مبتدأ keeps the precomposed hamza the print gives it.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَهَمَ الْخَلِيفَةَ هَذَا الْحَالُ قَالَ لَهُ أَيْنَ تَفْصِلُ فِي هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dahama al-khalīfata hādhā al-ḥālu qāla lahu ayna tafṣilu fī hādhihi al-sāʿati
sentences.l: And when overwhelmed the caliph this the-state, he said to-him: Where do-you-depart in this hour?
sentences.i: The plight of the young man overwhelmed the caliph, and he said to him, “Where will you go at this hour?”
sentences.n: The object comes first: دهم الخليفةَ هذا الحالُ, “this state came suddenly upon the caliph”, meaning that he was struck by it. تفصل is “you set out, depart” (فصل عن البلد); the print has no mark to say otherwise, and the sense fits.

sentences.t: قَالَ لَهُ بِلَادُاللَّهِ فَسِيحَةٌ
sentences.tr: qāla lahu bilādu Allāhi fasīḥatun
sentences.l: He said to-him: The lands of-God (are) spacious.
sentences.i: He answered, “God's lands are wide.”
sentences.n: The print joins بلاد الله into one word. The reply is a proverbial one: a man with nowhere to go is not without a place in the world.  The print has فسيحة with the ف as part of the word, and the next unit begins a new فقال.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْخَلِيفَةُ إِذَا كَتَبْتُ لَكَ وَرَقَةً تُؤَدِّيهَا إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ الزَّيْنِيِّ فَإِذَا قَرَأَهَا لَمْ يَضُرَّكَ بِشَيٌ وَلَا يُؤْذِيكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-khalīfatu idhā katabtu laka waraqatan tuʾaddīhā ilā al-sulṭāni Muḥammadi bni Sulaymāna al-Zayniyyi fa-idhā qaraʾahā lam yaḍurraka bi-shayʾin wa-lā yuʾdhīka
sentences.l: And said to-him the caliph: If I write for-you a paper, you-deliver-it to the sultan Muḥammad son-of Sulaymān al-Zaynī, then when he reads-it, he will-not harm-you in anything, and does-not hurt-you.
sentences.i: Then the caliph said to him, “If I write you a letter, and you carry it to the sultan Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Zaynī, then once he has read it he will do you no harm, and no hurt will come to you.”
sentences.n: Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Zaynī is the ruler of Basra, to whom the caliph proposes to send Nūr al-Dīn. The print marks the شيٌ with a tanwīn damma on the yā, which cannot be right after bi-; I keep the mark as printed and read the word as بِشَيْءٍ “in anything” (shayʾ). Likewise ولا يؤذيك has the indicative after لم … ولا, where Classical would repeat the jussive (ولا يؤذك); I vocalise what is printed, with the hamza on a wāw-seat. توديها is printed without its hamza; I read it as the second-form تُؤَدِّيهَا, “you deliver it” (from أدّى), the hamza sitting on the wāw.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُـــــــــــــبَـــــــــــــــاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And overtook Shahrazād the morning, and she fell-silent from the speech, the permitted.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.n: This is the closing formula of the night. The print stretches the last word with long tatweels, المـــبـــاح, which are kept; the pointing sits on the letters.
